lessons.title: A loop over an untyped array gives Variant elements, and an inferred type cannot come from them
lessons.symptom: Godot stops with a parse error: cannot infer the type of a variable because the value does not have a set type. It happened three times in one project, each time in code that looked fine.
lessons.cause: The loop variable of a literal array or an untyped Array has no static type, and neither has a value read from an untyped Dictionary or an untyped parameter. A variable whose type is inferred needs a typed value, so anything computed from them fails.
lessons.fix: Give the loop variable a type (for p: Vector3 in points), type the collection (Array[Vector3]), or write the type of the new variable instead of letting Godot infer it.

lessons.title: Check is_instance_valid() before anything else touches the object
lessons.symptom: Thousands of errors per run and a frame rate of about 6 fps: a queue of work items held one freed object, the call on it failed, and the queue never moved on.
lessons.cause: A type test, a typed local variable and a typed parameter all check the object as soon as they get it. On a freed object that check is itself the error, so an is_instance_valid() guard placed after it, or inside the called function, never runs.
lessons.fix: Read the item into a Variant, test is_instance_valid() first and the type after it, and advance a queue before calling into the item, so one bad item cannot block the rest.

lessons.title: A null default for get_meta() means no default
lessons.symptom: An engine error every time a mission started, although the code passed a default value.
lessons.cause: In Godot 4 a null default is treated as no default: when the entry is missing, get_meta() prints an error and returns null.
lessons.fix: Check has_meta() first, or pass a default that is not null.

lessons.title: Parsed data is null when the input is missing or broken
lessons.symptom: A black screen at start with no message on screen: a script error stopped the function that builds the world.
lessons.cause: JSON.parse_string() and str_to_var() return null for a missing or broken input. Assigning that straight to a typed Array or Dictionary is a runtime error, so the rest of the function never runs.
lessons.fix: Parse into a Variant, check it with is Array or is Dictionary, report what is wrong with push_error() and carry on without it.
errors: of type 'Nil' to a variable of type

lessons.title: Two patches or a merge can add the same function twice
lessons.symptom: A script that compiled before stops compiling after two candidate changes are combined.
lessons.cause: Both changes added the same helper functions, or a patch tool inserted a function that was already there. A class may declare each name once.
lessons.fix: Check the combined script before you ship it, and make patch tools check whether a function already exists before they add it.
errors: has the same name as a previously declared

lessons.title: An override must keep up when its parent gains a parameter
lessons.symptom: Parse error: the function signature does not match the parent, and every script that loads the child fails too.
lessons.cause: The base class got an extra optional parameter; the override still had the old list. An override may add trailing parameters that have defaults, never fewer than the parent.
lessons.fix: Give the override the same parameters as the parent, with the same defaults, and pass them on in the call to super.

lessons.title: A lambda that captures a node outlives the node
lessons.symptom: Errors that a lambda capture was freed, from timers that fired after their node was gone.
lessons.cause: A lambda keeps its captured values; when the node it captured is freed before the signal fires, the call fails.
lessons.fix: Connect a method of the node itself (for example its queue_free method as a Callable): Godot drops that connection when the node is freed.

lessons.title: Asserts are not checks in a release build
lessons.symptom: A check passed in testing and silently did nothing in the exported game; in another case a debug build stopped in a constructor and left a system half set up.
lessons.cause: Godot removes assert() from release builds, and in debug builds a failing assert stops the script.
lessons.fix: Use assert() only for programming mistakes in tests. For files, downloads and data, test with if and report with push_error().

lessons.title: Text encoded twice shows as garbage characters
lessons.symptom: Players saw two odd characters instead of one accented letter in the interface.
lessons.cause: The file was read as Latin-1 and written back as UTF-8, so every accented letter became two characters.
lessons.fix: Type the characters again and save the file as UTF-8; let tools that rewrite scripts read and write UTF-8.

lessons.title: Drawing calls only work inside _draw()
lessons.symptom: Errors that drawing is only allowed inside the draw callback, from a test that otherwise passed.
lessons.cause: A helper called draw_line() and friends on a canvas item from outside its _draw() callback.
lessons.fix: Call queue_redraw() and do the drawing in _draw() or in a function connected to the draw signal.

lessons.title: An infinite sentinel value must never reach a transform
lessons.symptom: About two thousand engine errors per run that a vector is not finite.
lessons.cause: A height meaning no ground below was kept as minus infinity and then used in a position.
lessons.fix: Guard every use of a sentinel with is_finite(), or keep a separate flag for no value.

lessons.title: Array.erase() on dictionaries inside a loop is quadratic
lessons.symptom: A hitch of 100 ms or more every time a part of the world was unloaded.
lessons.cause: Array.erase() compares dictionaries by content, so erasing many records one by one compares every record with every other.
lessons.fix: Mark the records to remove and filter the array once; in one case this took the work from 36 ms to 4 ms.

lessons.title: A float property never equals the 64-bit value you wrote
lessons.symptom: Settings were pushed to the rendering server every frame although nothing changed.
lessons.cause: Many engine properties are stored as 32-bit floats, while GDScript floats are 64-bit, so comparing the property with your value is almost never equal.
lessons.fix: Compare with is_equal_approx(), or remember the last value you wrote and compare with that.

lessons.title: An id taken from the size of a capped buffer stops counting
lessons.symptom: Event numbers stopped going up once the history was full, so new events looked like old ones.
lessons.cause: The id was the buffer size plus one, and the buffer drops its oldest entry when full.
lessons.fix: Keep a separate counter for ids.

lessons.title: Wrap a provider stored in metadata only once
lessons.symptom: A hard crash with a stack overflow when a player boarded a vehicle.
lessons.cause: Two systems each read a provider from metadata every second, kept it as their inner provider and put their own in its place, so each wrapped the other, again and again.
lessons.fix: Wrap once per target, never keep yourself as the inner provider, and add a busy guard.

lessons.title: A body placed on a moving platform must start at the platform's speed
lessons.symptom: A helicopter boarded on a ship sailing at 8 m/s slid 24 m off the stern in three seconds; on take-off and landing the deck slid away underneath it.
lessons.cause: The placing code set its velocity to zero, which is rest in the world, not on the deck. The brakes, the friction and the parked test also worked on world velocity.
lessons.fix: Start the body at the deck's velocity at that point (the deck velocity plus the angular velocity crossed with the offset), and run brakes, friction, parked tests and locks on the velocity relative to the deck.
lessons.test: Play the landing at rest, at cruise and at top speed, in calm and rough water and in turns: the body must slide less than 5 cm in 3 s after touchdown.

lessons.title: No collider of a ship may reach above its own landing deck
lessons.symptom: A parked helicopter bounced 1.1 m and seemed to land above the deck.
lessons.cause: The hull's collision box reached the height of the side walls across the whole beam, so it stood a metre above the helicopter deck and pushed the skids out every tick.
lessons.fix: End the hull box at deck level and give the walls their own thin boxes. Nothing may stand above a landing surface except declared obstacles, and the landing area must equal the collider's top.
lessons.test: For each declared landing surface, check that no other shape of the same body rises above its top within its footprint.

lessons.title: A landing pad that exists only as data cannot be landed on
lessons.symptom: An aircraft sank 0.29 m into a pad and was never on the floor.
lessons.cause: The pad was a height in a table, with no collision shape at that height.
lessons.fix: Every surface the player can stand or land on needs a collider at exactly its visible height.

lessons.title: Reset physics interpolation only after a teleport
lessons.symptom: A parked passenger shivered by up to 7 cm on a moving vehicle.
lessons.cause: With physics interpolation on, the passenger got reset_physics_interpolation() every tick, so it was drawn at its raw physics pose while the vehicle under it was drawn interpolated. The error is up to the speed divided by the tick rate.
lessons.fix: Call reset_physics_interpolation() only when a node jumps to a new place.

lessons.title: A camera that follows a body must read its interpolated pose
lessons.symptom: The cockpit slid up to half a metre against the eye at speed, and the heads-up display danced.
lessons.cause: With physics interpolation on, a body is drawn between two physics poses, but global_transform returns the last raw pose. A camera set from it in _process lags or leads the body.
lessons.fix: In _process, read get_global_transform_interpolated() from the body and turn physics interpolation off on the camera. Moving the camera into _physics_process does not fix it.

lessons.title: Carry a passenger on a platform in one way only
lessons.symptom: A person walking on a moving deck was carried twice as fast; after a fix, they no longer rode any platform at all.
lessons.cause: A script moved the passenger with the deck while CharacterBody3D also followed the platform it stood on. The fix set platform_floor_layers to 0 and never set it back.
lessons.fix: Keep one way of carrying. When your own code carries the body, save platform_floor_layers, set it to 0, and restore it when the carrying ends.

lessons.title: is_on_floor() is stale after code moves a body
lessons.symptom: The parked state flickered every tick, so the engine refused to start; there was a 4 cm hop at lift-off.
lessons.cause: is_on_floor() keeps the answer of the last move_and_slide(). After code sets the transform, it describes the old place. Flat contact shapes on a body that only turns about its vertical axis also dig into a tilted deck.
lessons.fix: Call apply_floor_snap() after moving the body by code, then restore its transform and velocity. Tilt the contact shapes to the deck, sink them about 3 mm, and use hysteresis for engage and release.

lessons.title: Many physics ticks per second can spiral down after one slow frame
lessons.symptom: The game ran at 3 to 5 fps for minutes, with up to 8 physics steps per frame.
lessons.cause: At 120 physics ticks per second with the default of up to 8 steps per frame, one slow frame makes Godot run many ticks to catch up, which makes the next frame slow as well.
lessons.fix: Lower max_physics_steps_per_frame to about 4, or run 60 ticks per second with physics interpolation on.
lessons.test: Measure physics steps per frame under load; more than two on average means the physics cost is too high for the tick rate.

lessons.title: A body riding a platform must update after the platform
lessons.symptom: Contacts with a moving deck were a tick behind, so bodies on it jittered or sank a little.
lessons.cause: The colliders of a body that a script moves sit at last tick's pose during the current tick, and riders that update first read the old deck.
lessons.fix: Update the platform before its riders (process_physics_priority) and stamp shared deck data with Engine.get_physics_frames(), so a rider knows the data is from this tick.

lessons.title: Reproduce a contact bug with the real body, under both physics engines
lessons.symptom: A mocked aircraft passed the landing test that the real one failed.
lessons.cause: The mock had other shapes, mass and damping than the real body, so the contact bug never showed.
lessons.fix: Reproduce the reported bug with the old code first, then fix it. Test with the real body under GodotPhysics3D and Jolt, at 60 and 120 ticks, and compare paths the fix should not touch with traces from before.
lessons.test: Run the same scenario with both physics engines and two tick rates, and compare the traces.

lessons.title: Change physics state inside overlap callbacks only deferred
lessons.symptom: An area that should switch off after a hit kept reporting, and Godot printed that it cannot change state while flushing queries.
lessons.cause: Godot reports overlaps while it walks its physics queries; adding physics nodes or switching monitoring at that moment is refused.
lessons.fix: Use add_child.call_deferred() and set_deferred() inside body and area entered or exited handlers.
errors: Can't change this state while flushing queries

lessons.title: Aim ballistic weapons with the projectile's own flight model
lessons.symptom: Aiming along the straight line to the target missed every ground target.
lessons.cause: A projectile with gravity and drag does not fly in a straight line; a straight aim is only right at very short range.
lessons.fix: Solve the elevation with the same physics the projectile uses; that hit within a metre.
lessons.test: A scenario that fires at targets at several ranges and checks the miss distance.

lessons.title: Slow motion must always be undone
lessons.symptom: After an impact camera, the whole game stayed slow.
lessons.cause: The effect lowered Engine.time_scale and only restored it when it finished normally, not when its node left the tree early.
lessons.fix: Set Engine.time_scale back to 1.0 when the effect ends and in _exit_tree().

lessons.title: Read positions from marker nodes, not from constants
lessons.symptom: Camera and muzzle positions broke every time the model changed.
lessons.cause: The positions were numbers in a script, so they no longer matched the new model.
lessons.fix: Put named marker nodes in the model and read their transforms at runtime.

lessons.title: Positions far from the origin lose precision; do not take velocities from them
lessons.symptom: At 28 km from the origin a speed jumped in steps of 0.23 m/s, and a turn rate read exactly zero, so a parked vehicle slid sideways in turns.
lessons.cause: Vector3 and Transform3D hold 32-bit floats: the step between two values is 0.12 mm at 1 to 2 km, 0.5 mm at 4 to 8 km and 2 mm at 16 to 32 km. A velocity taken from two positions is that step times the tick rate. The angle of a small rotation per tick rounds to zero below about 0.0005 radians.
lessons.fix: Keep the real state of fast or far objects in GDScript floats, which are 64-bit (speed, heading, height), and compute velocities from it. Get small rotations from the antisymmetric part of the rotation matrix, carry riders relative to the platform, and move the world origin when the player goes far.
lessons.test: Set test limits to at least ten times the float step at the largest distance in the world.

lessons.title: A chunk's visibility range is measured from its centre, so keep chunks small
lessons.symptom: Up to 136 million triangles drawn: whole tree chunks switched to their most detailed level at once.
lessons.cause: Trees were grouped in 256 m chunks with the detailed level up to 65 m, measured from the chunk's centre, so a camera inside a chunk drew all its trees in full detail.
lessons.fix: Make chunks no larger than the distance of their most detailed level, use visibility_parent for levels of detail, and skip nodes with a custom bounding box when you set ranges automatically.

lessons.title: Road, rail and waterway graphs must stay one connected network
lessons.symptom: Traffic got stuck at dead ends, and boats could not reach parts of the map after a new bridge.
lessons.cause: The traffic graph had parts not reachable from others, and a low bridge split the waterway network.
lessons.fix: Let traffic use only the strongly connected part of the graph, add turning loops at dead ends, check that the network is one piece after every edit, and rebuild derived graphs when the ground under them changes.

lessons.title: Simulate far-away things less often
lessons.symptom: A decorative ship far from the player cost 18 ms per frame; a fleet cost 3 ms per physics tick.
lessons.cause: Every object ran its full simulation every tick, and one asked for the full water surface five times per tick when it only needed the height.
lessons.fix: Use distance tiers (for example 30, 10 and 5 updates per second), freeze decorative objects beyond about 1.5 km, use the cheapest query that answers the question, and write transforms only when they change.
lessons.test: With the player 2 km away, the script time of far objects should be close to zero.

lessons.title: Textures loaded by a script get no mipmaps and no VRAM compression
lessons.symptom: Textures shimmered at a distance and video memory filled up: about a thousand textures took 10 GB.
lessons.cause: Godot only compresses textures and makes mipmaps when it imports them and sees them used in 3D. A glTF loaded at runtime, an ImageTexture made from an image, and a texture assigned from code all skip that.
lessons.fix: Generate mipmaps for runtime images (Image.generate_mipmaps(), with the normal map flag for normal maps), or bake models once into scenes with imported, compressed textures. Set textures used in 3D to VRAM compressed with mipmaps in their import settings.

lessons.title: An image read from its source file in the project is missing from the exported game
lessons.symptom: Textures that worked in the editor were missing after export.
lessons.cause: The export holds the imported texture, not the source image, so reading the image file fails; it also skips mipmaps and compression.
lessons.fix: Load the texture as a resource with load() and use it as a Texture2D.

lessons.title: Image.compress() for desktop formats only works in editor builds
lessons.symptom: Every attempt to compress textures at runtime failed in the exported game, while it worked in tests.
lessons.cause: The block compressors are part of the editor, not of export templates; the tests ran with the editor binary.
lessons.fix: Compress textures at import or build time, check is_compressed() at runtime, and run performance tests with the export template.

lessons.title: Block-compressed textures need sizes that are a multiple of 4
lessons.symptom: Some textures stayed uncompressed: 6 MB per map instead of 1.5 MB.
lessons.cause: A texture whose width or height is not a multiple of 4 cannot use the block formats, so it falls back to uncompressed.
lessons.fix: Use powers of two (1024, 2048, 4096), or at least multiples of 4.

lessons.title: A backup folder inside the project is imported again
lessons.symptom: Duplicate uids and a second import of the same model after an installer made a backup.
lessons.cause: Godot imports every folder under the project, backups included.
lessons.fix: Keep backups outside the project, or put an empty .gdignore file in the backup folder.

lessons.title: A copied project needs its import cache before scripts load
lessons.symptom: Headless scripts in a fresh copy failed on every class_name.
lessons.cause: The class list and the imported files live in the .godot folder, which a copy without it does not have.
lessons.fix: Import the project once (godot --headless --import) before running scripts in it.

lessons.title: Collision suffixes in node names only work in the editor importer
lessons.symptom: Collision proxies showed up as visible meshes in the game.
lessons.cause: Name suffixes that ask for collision shapes are read by the editor's scene importer; a glTF loaded at runtime keeps them as plain meshes.
lessons.fix: Build collision shapes yourself when you load a model at runtime, or import the model in the editor.

lessons.title: Small fill lights with cube shadows cost six passes each
lessons.symptom: A frame rate of 15 fps in a cockpit: five weak fill lights with a range of one or two metres cast shadows.
lessons.cause: An omni light's default shadow is a cube map, rendered six times; five lights made thirty shadow passes.
lessons.fix: Turn shadows off on small fill lights, or use the dual paraboloid shadow mode (two passes).

lessons.title: Vertex colours from colour codes need vertex_color_is_srgb
lessons.symptom: Generated terrain looked washed out and grey-blue.
lessons.cause: A colour written as a colour code is sRGB, but the material treats vertex colours as linear unless vertex_color_is_srgb is on.
lessons.fix: Turn on vertex_color_is_srgb when you use vertex colours as albedo.

lessons.title: Duplicate a material before you change it for one mesh
lessons.symptom: A whole group of meshes showed the detail texture that was meant for the last one.
lessons.cause: The meshes shared one material resource, so each change applied to all of them.
lessons.fix: Call duplicate() on the material and set the copy as the mesh's material_override.

lessons.title: Shader warm-up must use the same settings as the real view
lessons.symptom: Frames of half a second to five seconds after loading while new pipelines compiled.
lessons.cause: The warm-up view had no anti-aliasing or upscaling, while the game used them; pipelines depend on those settings.
lessons.fix: Warm up with the same anti-aliasing, scaling and effects as the main viewport.
lessons.test: After loading, the pipeline compilations per frame should stay at zero.

lessons.title: An animated sky shader must be cheap in its cubemap pass
lessons.symptom: About 8 fps with long stalls when clouds were in the sky.
lessons.cause: A sky shader that uses TIME is redrawn every frame, also for the radiance cubemap, and the cloud march ran at full resolution.
lessons.fix: Draw something cheap in the cubemap pass, march clouds at quarter resolution, and let the sky update the radiance map incrementally.

lessons.title: A water shader must not read the depth it writes itself
lessons.symptom: The water showed foam everywhere, and the floor behind it could not be reconstructed.
lessons.cause: With the alpha depth prepass, the water writes into the depth texture it then reads.
lessons.fix: Use depth_draw_always instead of the alpha prepass when a water shader reads the depth texture.

lessons.title: A mesh moved in its shader needs a bigger cull box
lessons.symptom: A waving flag popped out at the edge of the screen, and clouds disappeared far from the origin.
lessons.cause: Godot culls with the mesh's own box; vertices moved in the shader can leave it. A tool that set visibility ranges from that box gave a full-screen quad a range of a few kilometres.
lessons.fix: Set extra_cull_margin to at least the displacement, or a custom bounding box, and leave such meshes out of automatic visibility ranges.

lessons.title: Glass is opaque until you make it otherwise
lessons.symptom: A cockpit stayed hidden behind its windows, and thin see-through gaps showed around the panes.
lessons.cause: The glass material was opaque, or so nearly transparent and unlit that it vanished; panes were cut a few millimetres short of their opening.
lessons.fix: Give glass alpha blending with an alpha of about 0.15 to 0.3 and a low roughness, keep it a separate mesh, let the pane share the opening's edge, and give the interior behind it its own light.

lessons.title: The Compatibility renderer needs a fill light
lessons.symptom: The shaded side of a vehicle was almost black.
lessons.cause: Ambient light alone is weak in the Compatibility renderer.
lessons.fix: Add a soft directional or omni fill light, without shadows.

lessons.title: Gameplay scripts must not change global render settings
lessons.symptom: Three to five milliseconds of GPU time lost after one aircraft was used, and the level-of-detail setting changed on its own.
lessons.cause: A vehicle script set the main viewport's anti-aliasing and never set it back, and a sky script overwrote a setting the settings menu owned.
lessons.fix: Leave global render settings to the settings code; if an effect needs one, save the old value and restore it in _exit_tree().

lessons.title: A mirrored half needs its triangles reversed
lessons.symptom: The hull could be seen through from outside since the first version; a back-face render showed the inside-out parts.
lessons.cause: The generator mirrored one half by negating a coordinate. That turns every triangle the other way, but nobody reversed the vertex order, so Godot culled the outside.
lessons.fix: Reverse the triangle order and mirror the normals whenever a mesh is mirrored, or let the builder orient every triangle by its normal.
lessons.test: Render from 16 directions with back faces drawn in a loud colour; aim for almost none of that colour.

lessons.title: A level of detail must be much smaller than the one before it
lessons.symptom: The second level had 981 thousand triangles against 1 million for the first, and colours jumped when the level switched.
lessons.cause: The interior was kept in the lower levels, each part had its own reduction limit, and every level had its own copy of the materials.
lessons.fix: Keep lower levels to the outside only, reduce with one ratio (about a fifth per step), let all levels share the first level's materials by name and keep the same moving nodes in each. Count triangles from the final file.
lessons.test: Each level should have at most half the triangles of the one before it.

lessons.title: Node names that scripts use are a contract
lessons.symptom: Setting up a vehicle failed because a node did not exist, and new doors were missing from the list of moving parts.
lessons.cause: Scripts found nodes by exact name; the list of names came from an older build; Godot changes names with dots, colons and similar characters, and modelling tools add numbered suffixes to duplicates.
lessons.fix: Keep one spec as the single source of names, make the contract from the exported file, and check every level of detail and variant against it.

lessons.title: Check that a moving part turns the right way, not only about the right point
lessons.symptom: A control lever moved down when it was raised; the bug survived three versions. A mirrored rotor tilted inward instead of outward.
lessons.cause: Runtime code turned parts about a fixed local axis, but the node frame was built the other way round or mirrored.
lessons.fix: Write the axis and its positive direction into the contract, and in the builder turn each part by a test angle and check where its far end goes.

lessons.title: Put the origin where the model touches the ground
lessons.symptom: A model stood 1.4 m inside the ground.
lessons.cause: Its origin was at its centre, but the code placed it as if the origin were at the wheels.
lessons.fix: Put y = 0 at the wheels, skids or keel line, with +Y up, and check the lowest point is within a few millimetres of zero.

lessons.title: Measure the real thing before modelling
lessons.symptom: A published overall length was about 12 % off for the version being built, and the first model followed it.
lessons.cause: Sources describe different versions and measure different things; one number was taken as the truth.
lessons.fix: Scale photos on a part of known size and check against a second known size. Rate every source (official manual first, estimates last) and write down why when sources disagree. Generated drawings are good for shape only, never for size.

lessons.title: Keep one source of truth for the layout
lessons.symptom: Wheels ended up 0.35 m away from their axles after several builders worked in parallel.
lessons.cause: Each builder copied positions instead of reading them from one place.
lessons.fix: Keep one shared layout file that every part reads.

lessons.title: Compare silhouettes with photos, in the same pose
lessons.symptom: A shape check scored badly although the model was right.
lessons.cause: A raised launcher in the photo dominated the comparison, because the model was in its rest pose.
lessons.fix: Overlay the model's silhouette on a photo mask only when the pose matches.

lessons.title: Check the real finish before inventing one
lessons.symptom: A camouflage pattern looked right but was wrong; every reference showed one solid colour with wear.
lessons.cause: The finish was guessed from what such things usually look like.
lessons.fix: Look at references for colour and wear before texturing.

lessons.title: The width of a module is not the width of what it carries
lessons.symptom: A mounted module came out half as wide as the real one.
lessons.cause: The size from the manual described only the inner container, not the housings around it.
lessons.fix: Measure the visible outside of a module, not its payload.

lessons.title: Project details onto the mesh you actually render
lessons.symptom: Side consoles stood 4 cm outside the hull, an inner lining cut through the skin in hundreds of places, and trim floated 3 cm off it.
lessons.cause: Details were placed on a mathematical surface that differed from the lofted mesh that is drawn.
lessons.fix: Use one shape function for both, or project details onto the final mesh, and check that trim stays within a few millimetres of the skin.

lessons.title: Heavy models need levels of detail
lessons.symptom: A model of well over a million triangles was fine in a close-up and far too heavy as traffic.
lessons.cause: One level of detail served every distance.
lessons.fix: Set a budget per use: a hero helicopter about 350 to 600 thousand triangles outside plus its cockpit, a traffic car 22 to 70 thousand, with each lower level a fifth of the one above.

lessons.title: A model build should give the same file every time
lessons.symptom: Two builds of the same model had different checksums, so nobody could tell whether a change was intended.
lessons.cause: Noise was seeded with a hash that changes per process, and the export tool did not write the same bytes twice.
lessons.fix: Seed with a stable checksum of the name, write the file with a deterministic writer, and compare checksums of two builds.

lessons.title: Spread spawning, building and unloading over frames
lessons.symptom: Frames of 0.6 s to over a minute: seventeen vehicles and a hundred and thirty people spawned in one frame, a district of forty thousand nodes built at once, fifty physics bodies added in one step.
lessons.cause: Loading, instancing and adding nodes all happened on the main thread in one frame; freeing a big part also runs in one go.
lessons.fix: Request scenes early with ResourceLoader.load_threaded_request(), parse models on the WorkerThreadPool, add parts a few per frame (check is_inside_tree() after each await), and free large parts in small slices.
lessons.test: No frame over 100 ms in which the node count grows by more than a few hundred.

lessons.title: Parsing a glTF on the main thread costs about 13 to 15 ms per MB
lessons.symptom: A freeze of 2 to 5 seconds each time a vehicle appeared.
lessons.cause: The model was parsed, built and its textures read back from the GPU and uploaded again, all in one frame.
lessons.fix: Parse on a worker thread while the world loads, decode images from the file data instead of reading them back, and upload one texture per frame.

lessons.title: A retry timer must also run when the lookup found nothing
lessons.symptom: A search over the whole scene tree ran 120 times per second.
lessons.cause: The cached lookup retried whenever the node was missing, and the timer that should slow the retries only ran when it was found.
lessons.fix: Throttle the search itself: wait for the timer before every new search, whatever the last result was. Distance triggers need a minimum time between runs too, or they run every frame at high speed.

lessons.title: Pool effects instead of creating nodes per impact
lessons.symptom: Hundreds of particle, decal and light nodes per second in a firefight.
lessons.cause: Every hit created and freed its own nodes.
lessons.fix: Keep a few particle systems per effect and use emit_particle(), and reuse decals and lights from a pool; one burst then adds a handful of nodes instead of hundreds.

lessons.title: Redraw a heavy custom drawing only when it changes
lessons.symptom: A map screen took 45 ms per redraw and ran at 12 fps, because it redrew on every mouse move.
lessons.cause: queue_redraw() was called for every input event, and static layers were drawn again each time.
lessons.fix: Redraw only when something on it changed, and bake static layers into a mesh that is drawn with one call.

lessons.title: Reading a texture back from the GPU stalls the frame
lessons.symptom: Frames of 50 to 60 ms in the first minute, from hundreds of texture reads.
lessons.cause: get_image() on a texture waits for the GPU to copy it back.
lessons.fix: Keep the image you uploaded, or read it back asynchronously; never call get_image() in a loop over materials.

lessons.title: A headless test must be able to fail
lessons.symptom: Tests reported success while the log was full of script errors; one test hung forever.
lessons.cause: Godot exits with code 0 after a script error, the output went through a filter without pipefail, and a script error stopped the function before it could quit.
lessons.fix: Require an explicit pass line, scan the log for script and parse errors, compare errors with a known baseline, and add a watchdog or a frame limit.
lessons.test: Break the code on purpose once and see the test fail.

lessons.title: In a SceneTree test script, wait a frame before reading global positions
lessons.symptom: Over a hundred thousand errors that a node is not inside the tree, distances of minus 201 m and speeds of a million m/s.
lessons.cause: In _initialize() the nodes added to the root are not in the tree yet, so their global transforms are identity.
lessons.fix: Await process_frame after adding the scene and before the first check.

lessons.title: Verify with images, not with claims
lessons.symptom: Helpers reported that a model looked right when the render showed otherwise.
lessons.cause: No one looked at a picture before saying it was done.
lessons.fix: End every visual step with a render that is actually looked at, from fixed views.

lessons.title: Long background work can be lost
lessons.symptom: A restart of the machine stopped all running work.
lessons.cause: Results were only in memory or in the session.
lessons.fix: Write results to files as you go and resume from them.

lessons.title: Patch tools must match exactly once and undo everything on any error
lessons.symptom: Patches failed on files with Windows line endings, matched another feature's code, rewrote accented characters, or left a half-installed game after an interrupt.
lessons.cause: Anchors were plain text searches, encoding was not kept, and the backup was only restored for some errors.
lessons.fix: Make line endings the same before matching, require each anchor to match exactly once, keep the file's encoding, restore the backup on any error or interrupt, check for drift right before applying, and accept the result only when it has no new compile errors.

lessons.title: Measure performance with the export template, in alternating blocks
lessons.symptom: A fix that helped in tests did nothing in the game, and gates with a 5 % margin failed under normal load.
lessons.cause: Tests ran with the editor binary or headless, where some features differ and no frames are drawn; the measuring probes cost time themselves.
lessons.fix: Measure the exported game, switch a change on and off in alternating blocks and use the median, give gates enough margin, and note what the probes cost.

lessons.title: Give every change a switch to turn it off
lessons.symptom: Comparing with and without a change meant reinstalling the game.
lessons.cause: Changes were built in without a way to disable them.
lessons.fix: Let each change check a flag (a file or a setting) that turns it off, for comparisons and for a quick way back.

lessons.title: A cache key should hold only what the cached result depends on
lessons.symptom: A baked cache was thrown away on every install, adding 20 s to every cold start.
lessons.cause: The key hashed every script and the start location, so any change made a new cache.
lessons.fix: Hash only the code and the inputs the result depends on, and check stored values against fresh ones now and then.

lessons.title: Orphan-node and static-memory monitors always read 0 in a release export
lessons.symptom: A frame logger added columns for orphan nodes and static memory to explain long frames. In the game players ran, both columns were zero in every row, so long frames still had no explanation.
lessons.cause: Performance.OBJECT_ORPHAN_NODE_COUNT, MEMORY_STATIC and MEMORY_STATIC_MAX are only filled in debug builds. A game exported with the release template reports 0 for them, while the editor and debug exports show real values.
lessons.fix: Read these monitors only when OS.is_debug_build() is true. In release builds, log monitors that work there: OBJECT_NODE_COUNT, OBJECT_RESOURCE_COUNT, RENDER_VIDEO_MEM_USED and the pipeline compilation counters.
lessons.test: Run the logger once in a release export and fail when a column stays exactly 0 for the whole session.

lessons.title: Use the pipeline compilation monitors to tell shader stutter from loading hitches
lessons.symptom: Single frames of 0.9 to 3 s during play, and world starts of 40 to 80 s, fell outside script and physics time. No one could say whether shaders or synchronous loading caused them.
lessons.cause: Godot counts pipeline compilations by kind. PIPELINE_COMPILATIONS_DRAW happen while drawing and show up as stutter in play. PIPELINE_COMPILATIONS_MESH, PIPELINE_COMPILATIONS_SURFACE and PIPELINE_COMPILATIONS_CANVAS happen when resources load, which is harmless behind a loading screen. PIPELINE_COMPILATIONS_SPECIALIZATION runs in the background. A single total hides which kind it was.
lessons.fix: On every slow frame, log the change in each pipeline counter, in OBJECT_RESOURCE_COUNT and in RENDER_VIDEO_MEM_USED, plus DisplayServer.window_is_focused(). Draw compilations mean the shader warm-up is missing. New resources and a jump in video memory mean synchronous loading. No focus means the player switched windows, so the frame is not a game hitch.
lessons.test: Spawn an effect with a material that has never been drawn. The slow frame it causes must be classified as a draw compilation.

lessons.title: Split each frame into script, physics, deferred and draw time with probe nodes
lessons.symptom: Slow frames showed 3 to 6 physics steps, but the logs could not say whether physics caused them or followed from them. Many spikes landed in an unexplained remainder.
lessons.cause: The engine monitors give one total per phase per second and say nothing about the order of work inside a frame. Exported games have no profiler.
lessons.fix: Add a probe node with the lowest process_priority, which runs first in _process, and one with the highest, which runs last. Do the same with process_physics_priority, and time between the probes with Time.get_ticks_usec(). Time drawing with the RenderingServer.frame_pre_draw and frame_post_draw signals. Time deferred calls with your own call_deferred() at the end of _process, which runs after the calls queued before it. Measure GPU time per viewport with RenderingServer.viewport_set_measure_render_time().
lessons.test: Add one script that busy-waits 20 ms in _process and one that queues 300 ms of deferred work. Each must show up in its own column.

lessons.title: Profile _process per script in an exported game by giving script groups their own priorities
lessons.symptom: Every 2.6 s a burst of about 16 frames of 30 to 45 ms appeared, with 22 to 35 ms of it in _process. Switching script groups off one by one never pointed at a culprit.
lessons.cause: Release exports have no script profiler. Switching a group off changes the game, the switch itself can cause a hitch, and short periodic bursts slip through comparisons of block averages.
lessons.fix: Change no behaviour. For a short window, give each script group its own process_priority (10, 20, 30 and so on, in the original order) and put a timing node between the groups (15, 25 and so on). The time between two timing nodes is that group's _process cost in that frame. Restore the old priorities afterwards.
lessons.test: Add a group that busy-waits 5 ms every 40th frame. The profile must name it as the source of the burst.

lessons.title: An on/off cost scan that compares medians misses periodic spikes, so count spike frames too
lessons.symptom: A tool that switched script groups off for a block of frames first credited every group with an 11 to 14 ms gain. Later it found nothing while the game stuttered six times a second.
lessons.cause: The baseline was measured once, right after the key press, during a short spike. A median per block ignores a few 40 ms frames, and a periodic stutter is exactly that. Switching some groups off or on also caused a 1 to 2 s hitch by itself.
lessons.fix: Wait about a second, then alternate ON, OFF and ON blocks and compare each OFF block with the ON blocks right before and after it. Report the noise, and call a gain certain only when it is above twice the noise. Also count frames above max(25 ms, twice the median) in each block, and name the group whose OFF block removes them. Flag any group whose switch produced a frame over 250 ms, and repeat the scan when the start and end baselines differ by more than 1 ms.
lessons.test: Add a group that spikes 40 ms every 10 frames and a group that costs a constant 1 ms. The scan must name both, each with the right kind of cost.

lessons.title: A diagnostic that walks the whole scene tree in one frame causes the hitches it reports
lessons.symptom: The frame logger itself produced these frames: 433 ms when the report key was pressed, 0.7 to 1.1 s fifteen seconds after every start (a texture count over all geometry), 110 to 150 ms for each heavy-frame dump, and 1 s every 120 s from a background texture scan.
lessons.cause: A visit to every node, every GeometryInstance3D and every material in one frame costs as much as the worst gameplay hitch in a large world. Automatic periodic scans then add those hitches to every session.
lessons.fix: Walk the tree with an explicit stack in slices. Use a time budget of about 2 ms per frame, or a fixed number of nodes per frame (300 to 400 geometry instances), and finish the report over several frames. Mark the frames in which a scan ran so the report does not blame the game for them, and give automatic scans an off switch.
lessons.test: In a scene of 50 thousand nodes, a frame during the scan may take only a few ms more than the baseline. Here the report frame went from 433 ms to about 57 ms.

lessons.title: A while loop that waits for a state another method may refuse to set freezes the game
lessons.symptom: The game froze completely when the player switched weapons while airborne.
lessons.cause: Weapon selection looped until the current mode equalled the requested one, calling the cycle method on each pass. That method refused to cycle in the air, so the condition never changed and the main thread spun forever.
lessons.fix: Limit such loops to the number of possible states, check that each call changed something, and tell the player when the target cannot be reached.
lessons.test: Request every mode in every state where cycling is refused, and check that the call returns.

lessons.title: RigidBody3D has linear_velocity, not velocity, so duck-typed code that reads velocity breaks on it
lessons.symptom: A carrier landing system written for character-style aircraft could not arrest a jet that was a rigid body.
lessons.cause: The arresting code read the velocity property of whatever object it was given. CharacterBody3D has velocity, but RigidBody3D only has linear_velocity, so the read is an error on a rigid body (or null through get()).
lessons.fix: Read the velocity through one helper that checks the class: linear_velocity for RigidBody3D, velocity for CharacterBody3D. Alternatively, give the rigid body a small child node that exposes velocity and copies linear_velocity every physics tick, and pass that node to the system.
lessons.test: Run the same arrest test with both body types.

lessons.title: A conformal HUD must redraw every frame, or its symbols judder against the world
lessons.symptom: The head-up display of a jet stuttered against the view outside.
lessons.cause: To save time, the HUD's _draw() was triggered only 12.5 times per second. Its symbols, such as the flight path marker, the pitch ladder and the horizon, are tied to the outside world, which moves every frame.
lessons.fix: Call queue_redraw() every frame for world-locked symbols, and make the drawing itself cheap instead. Keep the throttle only for pages that show plain numbers or static text.
lessons.test: Record a roll at a constant rate. The horizon line must move by the same amount in every frame.

lessons.title: A particle vector field texture is read as rgb*2-1, with image row 0 at the bottom of the box
lessons.symptom: A generated 3D wind field for rotor downwash worked only after its encoding had been tested in the engine. The class reference does not say how colours map to vectors or which image row is which end of the box.
lessons.cause: The vector field attractor for GPUParticles3D samples its Texture3D across the attractor box. A channel value c becomes the vector component c*2-1, so 0.5 means no push. With a positive strength, particles are pushed along that vector. Row 0 of each image layer is the bottom (-Y) of the box, and the layer index runs along Z.
lessons.fix: Store each vector as v*0.5+0.5 in an RGBF image, fill rows from the bottom of the box upwards, keep the resolution close to the box size, and build the Texture3D once and reuse it.
lessons.test: Put a single upward vector in the bottom row only, and check that only particles near the floor of the box rise.

lessons.title: Do not use COLOR for albedo on MultiMesh foliage that also uses custom data
lessons.symptom: Trees drawn as MultiMesh instances turned blue or yellow in the Compatibility renderer, while Forward+ looked right.
lessons.cause: The tree shader multiplied the albedo by COLOR, which held a near-white vertex colour. The MultiMesh also used per-instance custom data, and in the Compatibility renderer instance data was seen arriving in COLOR instead of the vertex colour.
lessons.fix: Do not multiply albedo by COLOR on instanced foliage. Use a constant or bake the tint into the texture, and pass per-instance values only through the instance custom data. Render every shader in each renderer you ship.
lessons.test: Render the same forest in Compatibility and in Forward+ and compare the average hue.

lessons.title: Use find_children() with owned set to false instead of a recursive GDScript walk
lessons.symptom: A ground marshal collected the collision objects of a whole aircraft, cockpit included, with a recursive GDScript function on every physics tick while the aircraft stood on the pad. Elsewhere, a full tree search for one node ran every second over 85 thousand nodes.
lessons.cause: A recursive walk in GDScript makes one script call per node and is slow on deep models. The native Node.find_children() is much faster, but its owned parameter defaults to true, and then it skips nodes without an owner, such as nodes added by code.
lessons.fix: Call find_children() with the pattern "*", the class name, recursive true and owned false. Cache the result until the tree changes, and search for single nodes rarely (for example every 20 s) or keep a reference.
lessons.test: On a model with children added at runtime, compare the result with the old walk: same nodes, in the same pre-order.

lessons.title: Wait for worker tasks and threaded loads before the node that started them leaves the tree
lessons.symptom: The world crashed when it was freed, or when the player went back to the menu, while trees were still being built in the background.
lessons.cause: WorkerThreadPool tasks and loads started with ResourceLoader.load_threaded_request() kept running and wrote into objects that were being freed. The class reference also asks for every WorkerThreadPool task to be waited for once, so that it can be cleaned up.
lessons.fix: In _exit_tree(), stop starting new work, call WorkerThreadPool.wait_for_task_completion() for every running task, and call ResourceLoader.load_threaded_get() for every request still in progress, which blocks until it is done. Only then let the node go. Give each task a static function of the script plus plain data, never a method of a node that may be freed while the task runs.
lessons.test: In a headless test, leave the world in the middle of streaming a hundred times. There must be no crash and no errors.

lessons.title: Filter procedural instances where they are placed, not with a cleanup pass afterwards
lessons.symptom: Trees and grass flashed up on a high-speed rail line. Some trees stood on the track for up to two seconds after each new cell loaded, and other generators did not know about the track at all.
lessons.cause: One system placed trees per cell, and a second system removed the ones near the track every 2 s with a 4 m margin. The trees in towns and the ground cover came from other generators that had no exclusion strip.
lessons.fix: Give every placement generator the same exclusion test (distance to track, roads, buildings and water) and apply it before an instance is written, before set_instance_transform() on the MultiMesh. Use a margin wider than the crown radius (here 14 to 16 m for trees), and let ground cover wait until the exclusion data is ready.
lessons.test: Count instances inside the corridor right after each cell loads. The count must be zero.

lessons.title: Round a fast track's height profile with vertical curves, or every grade change feels like a speed bump
lessons.symptom: A high-speed train jolted at dozens of points along its line at 375 km/h, most of all near tunnel mouths.
lessons.cause: The track height followed sampled terrain and tunnel depth targets with straight segments. At high speed, each change of grade is a sudden vertical acceleration.
lessons.fix: After sampling, fit vertical curves with a minimum radius (about 15 km or more for very high speed) and spread grade changes at tunnel mouths over several hundred metres. Measure the remaining kinks against that radius after every change to the layout.
lessons.test: List every point where the local vertical radius is below the minimum. Here the count went from 75 to 11, and the rest were known exceptions.

lessons.title: Count overlaps between generated layers, then resolve them by moving, shrinking and only then removing
lessons.symptom: Thousands of houses stood on roads or inside each other, trees grew through houses and stood in water, and lamp posts stood on the carriageway.
lessons.cause: The roads, buildings, trees and street lamps came from separate generators that never tested against each other's footprints.
lessons.fix: Write a census that counts each kind of overlap: house and road, house and house, tree and house, lamp and carriageway, anything and water or track. Resolve in this order: move the object, shrink it, and remove it only as a last step. Run the census again and ship only at zero.
lessons.test: After the fix, the census shows zero overlaps in every class.

lessons.title: Effects that hide or destroy everything in an area must use an opt-in group
lessons.symptom: A big explosion hid the 3D cloud layer. A vehicle mode that hid every HUD layer also hid the pause menu and the minimap.
lessons.cause: The sweeps took every node within a radius, or every CanvasLayer, and skipped only a hard-coded list of exceptions. Every new shared system, such as the sky, a menu or the minimap, was caught by default.
lessons.fix: Let nodes declare that a sweep may affect them, with a group such as destructible or vehicle HUD, and sweep only that group. Keep an exception list only as a fallback.
lessons.test: Add a dummy shared node near the blast or under a CanvasLayer and run the sweep. It must stay visible.

lessons.title: Composite volumetric clouds against the scene depth, not against a fixed distance
lessons.symptom: An object about 40 m from the camera, exactly where a follow camera sat behind a missile, kept jumping in front of and behind a cloud.
lessons.cause: The cloud compositing pass treated everything nearer than a fixed 40 m as in front of the clouds and everything else as behind them.
lessons.fix: Rebuild the distance of the opaque pixel from the depth texture and compare it with the points where the view ray enters and leaves the cloud layer. When the object is in front of the entry point, draw no cloud. When it is beyond the exit point, draw the full cloud. When it is inside the layer, march only up to the object and scale the cloud colour and alpha by that partial opacity.
lessons.test: Fly a camera through the cloud base with an object at a fixed offset. The object must not pop.

lessons.title: Use surface override materials instead of duplicating a big mesh to change its materials
lessons.symptom: Spawning a detailed train cab took about 6 s.
lessons.cause: Each spawn called duplicate() on large baked meshes to give them their own materials, which copied all vertex data on the main thread. The textures were also loaded at spawn time.
lessons.fix: Share the mesh and set materials with MeshInstance3D.set_surface_override_material(). Request the meshes with ResourceLoader.load_threaded_request() and prepare the textures on the WorkerThreadPool while the world loads. Here the spawn took about 3 s afterwards, with an identical image.
lessons.test: Compare a render checksum before and after the change (it must be identical) and time the spawn.

lessons.title: 2D lines baked into a mesh need MSAA, and lines thinner than 1 px flicker
lessons.symptom: After a map's line layers were baked into meshes for speed, the edges looked jagged, and contour lines of 0.75 px flickered while the map moved.
lessons.cause: draw_line() and draw_polyline() with antialiasing add their own soft edges, but a mesh drawn with draw_mesh() gets none. A line thinner than a pixel covers pixels on and off as it moves.
lessons.fix: Turn on msaa_2d (4x) on the SubViewport that draws the map. Draw lines at least 1 px wide and lower their alpha instead of making them thinner. Until a baked mesh is ready, keep drawing the layer the old way.
lessons.test: Pan the map by one pixel per frame and compare frames. Thin lines must not appear and disappear.

lessons.title: Write UI text, layout and shader parameters only when they change, even on hidden controls
lessons.symptom: A profiler found 0.38 ms per frame in a small HUD script and about 1 ms in a few weapon mounts and beacon lights, much of it while the controls were hidden or the objects were far away.
lessons.cause: The scripts built strings and assigned Label.text, position, size and shader parameters every frame, including for a banner that was always hidden. A changed string is shaped again, and every set_shader_parameter() call updates the material.
lessons.fix: Keep the last value you wrote and assign only when the new value differs. Update the text of hidden labels at most a few times per second. Set material parameters only when the state changes, for example when a light flashes on or off.
lessons.test: Profile the script with the control hidden and the object far away, before and after the change.

lessons.title: Test a patch against the shipped game by mounting it as an extra pack, and run the same test without it
lessons.symptom: A new aircraft passed its own tests, but against the game players had it produced a script error every frame, because the package held an older version of a script it called. Other tests failed for reasons unrelated to the patch, such as key bindings saved on the test machine.
lessons.cause: Tests ran against copies instead of the files players actually have, and there was no run without the patch to separate old failures from new ones.
lessons.fix: Run the shipped .pck with --main-pack. Pack the changed files with PCKPacker and mount them with ProjectSettings.load_resource_pack(), replacing files, before anything loads those paths. Run the same test once without the pack as a baseline. Point the user data folder (the XDG data, config and cache variables on Linux) at a fresh temporary folder so saved settings cannot affect the result.
lessons.test: The patched run must show the baseline failures, minus the ones the patch fixes, and no new ones.

lessons.title: A render check in a different renderer than the game uses is not proof
lessons.symptom: Test renders in the Compatibility renderer were too dark to judge fine cockpit detail, some trees had wrong colours only there, and a shader warm-up could not be checked headless at all.
lessons.cause: The game ran Forward+ on Vulkan, while the checks ran headless or with the OpenGL rendering driver. Headless runs do no GPU work, so pipeline counters and render times stay at zero. Compatibility differs in lighting, depth range and some shader inputs.
lessons.fix: Run visual and warm-up checks with the game's renderer. Without a GPU, use a software Vulkan driver such as lavapipe under a virtual display. Write the renderer into every result, and do not call a visual change done on the strength of a Compatibility render alone.
lessons.test: Every report logs the renderer it used. A visual pass from a different renderer is not accepted.

lessons.title: Find holes in a cockpit or cabin by rendering it against a magenta background
lessons.symptom: Gaps between glass, trim and floor, such as an opening behind the pedals into the nose bay, did not show in normal renders because something dark was behind them.
lessons.cause: With a sky and a ground plane behind the model, a hole shows a plausible colour and nothing flags it.
lessons.fix: Render the interior from the eye points with the background set to plain magenta (Environment.background_mode set to a colour), flat grey ambient light, no ground, and the glass hidden. Every magenta pixel is a hole. Count them per view and require zero.
lessons.test: Count magenta pixels per fixed view after every model change.

lessons.title: When you replace one step of a seeded generator, keep its random draws or everything after it moves
lessons.symptom: When simple forest meshes were swapped for detailed trees in a seeded area, that could have moved every object generated after the forest, such as patrol routes and buildings, because all steps drew from one random number generator.
lessons.cause: A RandomNumberGenerator gives a sequence. A step that takes more or fewer numbers shifts every later draw, so later steps place things elsewhere.
lessons.fix: Make the new step take exactly the same number and order of draws as the old one, and add its own extra randomness from a separate generator. Better, give each step its own RandomNumberGenerator seeded from a stable hash of its name.
lessons.test: Compare RandomNumberGenerator.state, or a hash of all later positions, after the step with the old version. They must be identical.

lessons.title: When automation brakes, blocks or ignores the player, show and log why
lessons.symptom: Players reported that the train suddenly stopped for no reason, and a mode switch key on a jet sometimes did nothing.
lessons.cause: The train protection braked correctly for a red signal caused by an AI train ahead in the same block, but nothing on screen said so. The jet refused the switch outside its speed range without a message. A correct reaction looked like a bug.
lessons.fix: For every automatic intervention or refusal (signal, speed restriction, emergency brake, refused action), show one short message with its cause, and write a log line with time, position and cause. The next report can then be answered from the log.
lessons.test: Script a red signal ahead and a refused action, and check for one message and one log line each.

lessons.title: In an arcade flight model, let the stick set a bank angle, not a roll rate
lessons.symptom: In aeroplane mode, a tiltrotor rolled to 65 degrees in two seconds in a turn and sank into the ground. Players said it could not be flown.
lessons.cause: Stick deflection commanded a roll rate, so holding the stick kept the aircraft rolling, and lift was not increased for the bank, so altitude fell.
lessons.fix: Let the stick set a target bank angle (for example up to 40 degrees, back to level when released), hold altitude and heading while the stick is centred, and add the extra lift a banked turn needs.
lessons.test: Hold full stick for 10 s in a scripted flight. The bank must stay at the limit and the height within about 5 m.

lessons.title: Compare old and new results over thousands of inputs to prove a speed-up changes nothing
lessons.symptom: The physics of a fleet of ships cost 2.5 to 3.4 ms per physics tick, and the wave sampler had to be made faster without changing anything that reads the sea, including deterministic deck predictions.
lessons.cause: Small rewrites of float code, such as computing a coastline term once instead of three times or removing intermediate dictionaries, can change the last bits of results and shift a deterministic simulation over time.
lessons.fix: Keep the same formulas in the same order. Run the old and the new function side by side over thousands of samples (here 10 thousand points in four weather states) and require bit-equal results. Only then time both versions. Here this gave about 11 % per sample with identical motion.
lessons.test: Keep the comparison as a test that loads both versions of the script and fails on the first difference.

lessons.title: A short camera far plus thick exponential fog gives a grey wall, not distance haze
lessons.symptom: A grey fog wall with a hard edge and blue gaps a few kilometres out. Distant hills and the far terrain levels, built out to 24-36 km, never showed. Volumetric fog made a second haze wall right in front of the camera.
lessons.cause: The main Camera3D.far was 7.6 km, so everything beyond it was culled, and exponential fog at density 0.0007 is already 99.5 % opaque at that distance. Volumetric fog at density 0.012 over its default 64 m volumetric_fog_length concentrates all of its haze in the first metres.
lessons.fix: Raise far only on the cameras that need it (the main view, above water). Convert the raw density the weather writes into a visual range and use Environment.fog_mode = FOG_MODE_DEPTH with fog_depth_begin, fog_depth_end and fog_depth_curve; in depth mode fog_density scales the maximum, so a value around 0.8 in clear weather keeps ridges, coasts and towns as silhouettes, and 1.0 in fog or rain closes it. Add fog_aerial_perspective so far geometry takes the sky colour. Make volumetric fog thin and long (256-512 m). Always convert from the raw weather value so the conversion never stacks on its own output.
lessons.test: Render the same view in clear, overcast and foggy weather before and after: in clear weather terrain at 20-30 km keeps some contrast, in fog it still disappears.

lessons.title: A larger Camera3D.far draws every node without a visibility range out to the new distance
lessons.symptom: A follow camera for a fast missile got a far of 60 km: up to 690,000 objects in view and about 10,000 draw calls. Moving the main view's far from 7.6 to 40 km threatened the same for small props and forests.
lessons.cause: Distance culling only comes from the camera's far plane and each GeometryInstance3D's visibility_range_end. Nodes left at the default of 0 have no distance limit, so a bigger far pulls every small object in the world into the frame.
lessons.fix: Derive far from what the shot needs (for example altitude x 2.5 + 9 km, at least 9 km) and restore it afterwards. Before raising far for the whole game, give small objects (under a few hundred metres across) and forest MultiMesh nodes that have no range of their own a visibility_range_end near the old far with a fade margin, in a scan with a time budget per frame. Never overwrite ranges other code has set, and leave cameras that deliberately look far alone.
lessons.test: Compare Performance RENDER_TOTAL_OBJECTS_IN_FRAME and draw calls at the same view before and after raising far.

lessons.title: Requesting HDR output does nothing while the tonemapper or glow mode is SDR-only
lessons.symptom: With HDR switched on in the settings menu the picture looked exactly like SDR.
lessons.cause: Window.hdr_output_requested only asks for HDR output. The world Environment used TONE_MAPPER_FILMIC (and ACES in places), which produce SDR-range output, glow used GLOW_BLEND_MODE_SOFTLIGHT, which is SDR-only, and a colour-correction LUT is SDR-only too. On Windows the project only got HDR with the d3d12 rendering driver; with Vulkan the request was reported as unsupported.
lessons.fix: When DisplayServer.window_is_hdr_output_enabled() turns true, switch every Environment (WorldEnvironment and Camera3D environments, including ones added later) to TONE_MAPPER_AGX, glow to GLOW_BLEND_MODE_SCREEN, switch the LUT off and set use_hdr_2d on every full-screen SubViewport; restore the saved SDR values when HDR goes off. Expose paper white and peak through window_set_hdr_output_reference_luminance() and window_set_hdr_output_max_luminance(), check window_is_hdr_output_supported(), and offer the d3d12 rendering driver as a launch option.
lessons.test: Headless: fake the HDR state and check that tonemapper, glow mode and LUT switch and are restored. Then look at it on a real HDR screen.

lessons.title: A SubViewport set to UPDATE_ALWAYS renders every frame, even when nobody can see it
lessons.symptom: A jet's five cockpit screens, its full-screen HUD layer and its sensor camera view kept rendering in the outside views, costing frame time for images no one looked at.
lessons.cause: render_target_update_mode = UPDATE_ALWAYS forces a render each frame whether or not its ViewportTexture is on screen. A sensor SubViewport with its own Camera3D renders the whole 3D world a second time.
lessons.fix: Set UPDATE_DISABLED while the view that shows them is not active. Render slow instrument pages round-robin with UPDATE_ONCE (each screen every third frame when they redraw at about 12 Hz anyway) and keep a conformal HUD at full rate. Render a sensor view only while its page is open, at half rate on small displays. Size each SubViewport to the aspect ratio of the screen mesh instead of stretching a square one. Keep a switch that restores always-on rendering.
lessons.test: Count how many SubViewport nodes requested a render per frame and compare frame time inside and outside the cockpit.

lessons.title: A full-screen overlay does not stop the 3D world underneath from rendering
lessons.symptom: In the orbit view the frame cost stayed as high as near the ground, although the world below was completely covered by the space scene.
lessons.cause: The space scene was drawn in two SubViewport nodes composited over the main view, but the main Viewport kept rendering terrain, towns, sea and clouds behind it, and both of them also rendered while the overlay was faded out.
lessons.fix: When the overlay is fully opaque, set the main Viewport.disable_3d = true and restore the previous value when it fades again; keep the overlay SubViewport nodes at UPDATE_DISABLED while hidden and resize them to the window when shown.
lessons.test: Measure GPU frame time with the overlay fully covering the view; it should drop to the overlay's own cost.

lessons.title: A camera moved in frame_pre_draw reaches the renderer one frame late unless you force its transform
lessons.symptom: The whole cockpit interior shook against the view every frame, by up to one full physics tick of motion at 120 Hz physics.
lessons.cause: Node3D transform changes are collected and sent on when the scene tree flushes its transform notifications after _process. RenderingServer.frame_pre_draw runs after that flush, so a Camera3D pose set there only reaches the renderer in the next frame, while the cockpit is already drawn at the newer interpolated pose.
lessons.fix: Call force_update_transform() on the camera right after setting its global_transform inside a frame_pre_draw handler, or set the pose in _process once the vehicle's interpolated pose is known.
lessons.test: Log the camera-to-cockpit offset every frame during a hard turn; it must stay constant.

lessons.title: Terrain skirts and coarse LODs poke into shallow tunnels; cut holes in every terrain material
lessons.symptom: Inside rail tunnels and underground station halls you saw patches of ground and other terrain textures.
lessons.cause: Only the near terrain shader discarded fragments inside tunnel volumes. The vertical edge strips between terrain chunks (45 m deep), and the skirts and coarse LOD of the far terrain, had their own materials and hung down into shallow tunnels; a covered tunnel shell also showed through the coarse terrain LOD from far away.
lessons.fix: Keep all tunnel volumes in one data texture (rectangles plus a grid index, one texture fetch per fragment) and apply the same discard in every terrain material, including far, skirt and edge materials and ones created later; re-check every few seconds that the holes are still applied after a material swap. Hide tunnel shells beyond a short distance.
lessons.test: Check every crossing of a tunnel with chunk edges and far-terrain cells, then fly a camera through each tunnel and look for terrain pixels.

lessons.title: queue_free() of a big subtree costs its whole delete at the end of the frame, outside every script
lessons.symptom: At 370 km/h a train hitched every 10 s (one track tile per kilometre): frames of 48-55 ms with 43-45 ms spent after _process, while no script's own timing showed the cost.
lessons.cause: An old detail tile far behind the train was dropped with one queue_free() on a node holding thousands of children. Godot deletes the whole subtree in the deferred delete flush at the end of the frame, so the time lands after _process instead of in the script that asked for it.
lessons.fix: Hide the tile at once, then free its children directly a few at a time under a per-frame time budget (about 1.5 ms) and free the parent last. Keep a switch to fall back to the old behaviour.
lessons.test: Headless: a parent with 40 children is hidden in the same frame and fully freed over the next frames. In the game: no frame above 45 ms with more than 30 ms of after-process time at full speed.

lessons.title: Thousands of small identical meshes cost about 0.1 ms each to commit; draw them as one MultiMesh
lessons.symptom: A station coming into range caused an 872 ms frame with 1,500 new nodes. One underground hall took 550 ms to build, 290 ms of which was committing about 2,700 separate tactile-strip ribs.
lessons.cause: Every rib was its own small cylinder mesh committed to its own MeshInstance3D on the main thread, so the cost grew with the count; the many floors of the interchange were also built in one frame.
lessons.fix: Put repeated identical parts in one MultiMeshInstance3D with a shared mesh and per-instance transforms (same positions, size, colour and material). Build big structures far from the camera over several frames (about 3 ms per frame) and only build synchronously when the camera is close.
lessons.test: Headless over all stations: longest build call before and after (here 756 ms to 36 ms), and an identical scene-tree hash afterwards.

lessons.title: Fast-forward with Engine.time_scale speeds up, and costs, the whole world, not just what you watch
lessons.symptom: Switching a missile follow view to 2x or 4x time dropped the game to 3-20 fps with 8 physics steps per frame.
lessons.cause: Engine.time_scale scales the delta of every process and physics step, so everything in the world advances faster at once. Code that substeps by delta does more work per tick, frames get slower, and the physics catch-up loop then runs up to Engine.max_physics_steps_per_frame steps per frame (about 3.5 ms per step was measured).
lessons.fix: Leave Engine.time_scale at 1. Fast-forward only the followed objects by calling their own physics step extra times per tick, and lower Engine.max_physics_steps_per_frame (for example to 4) while that view is open, restoring the saved value when it closes.
lessons.test: Measure frame time and physics steps per frame at 1x and 4x in the same scene; at 4x only the followed object's cost should grow.

lessons.title: A check like int(t * k) % n == 0 is true for a whole window of frames, not once
lessons.symptom: Every 2.5 s came half a second of 28 ms frames; a profile pointed 48 of 49 slow frames at one small prop script.
lessons.cause: A test meant to run every 2.5 s took the integer part of time x 2 modulo 5, which stays at 0 for half a second, so an expensive find_children() over the whole tree (about 90,000 nodes) ran on every frame of that window.
lessons.fix: Use a countdown (subtract delta, act when it reaches zero, then reset it) or compare with the time of the last run. Cache the node you search for and only search again after a delay when it has gone.
lessons.test: Count how often the expensive branch runs per second; it must match the intended rate exactly.

lessons.title: A ternary used as a statement to choose between two void calls does not compile
lessons.symptom: A one-line ternary that called add_child() on one of two parents gave a parse error, and the whole script failed to load, not just that line.
lessons.cause: In GDScript a ternary is an expression, so both branches must give a value. add_child() returns void, so the analyzer rejects using its result, and one compile error stops every function in the file.
lessons.fix: Use an if/else statement to choose between actions. Use a ternary only to choose a value, for example pick the parent with it and call add_child() once.
lessons.test: Load every changed script headless and check can_instantiate(); a review rule can flag a ternary that stands alone on a line.

lessons.title: A name check cannot catch a node added twice: Godot renames the second one
lessons.symptom: A check meant to stop an overlay from being applied twice let the second application through, and two copies ended up in the cockpit.
lessons.cause: add_child() gives a node whose name is already taken by a sibling a new name, with a number appended, or an @-wrapped generated name unless readable names are forced. Comparing child names with the intended name never matches the duplicate.
lessons.fix: Mark the nodes you add with set_meta() and count marked direct children, or keep a reference to what you added and check it with is_instance_valid() before adding again.
lessons.test: Apply the overlay twice in a test and assert exactly one marked child.

lessons.title: A landed aircraft must not keep integrating attitude from the stick; blend authority in with height
lessons.symptom: Every helicopter standing on a pad or a ship's deck rolled up to 64 degrees and pitched 46 degrees when the player moved the mouse or stick.
lessons.cause: The flight model integrated roll and pitch from cyclic input in every state and on the ground only damped the rates, so input kept rotating the body while the skids were on the ground.
lessons.fix: Give each axis an authority factor from 0 to 1: 0 on the ground or locked to a deck without a lift command (level the body at a fixed rate, zero the rates); rising with height above the lift-off point (full roll at about 1.2 m, pitch at 0.8 m) with a rate limit; fading out over the last metre when landing. Keep it exactly 1 in the air so handling does not change, and keep terrain and deck slope as a visual offset.
lessons.test: A scripted test with the real body on a floor and full stick: 0.00 degrees roll and pitch on the ground, a gradual bank after lift-off (no step above about 0.12 degrees per tick), unchanged handling in the air, level again after landing.

lessons.title: NPC followers must keep more distance than the length of what their leader carries
lessons.symptom: A medical crew carrying a stretcher to a helicopter froze at the scene in 7 of 8 scenarios; on longer routes the stretcher vanished halfway.
lessons.cause: The followers followed the carrier at 2.5 m, but the foot end of the stretcher trails 2.2 m behind the carrier, so the followers stood in its path. When the gap to the foot end grew beyond 3.1 m the carry logic stopped the carrier for good. A fixed carry timeout of 300 s (about 300 m at walking pace) also expired on longer walks.
lessons.fix: Put followers behind the load (6 m), derive the timeout from the distance (distance / speed + a margin), and add a watchdog for the carry phase: if the trailing end lags for 5 s, put it back behind the carrier; if the carrier has not moved for 15 s while far from the goal, move it a few metres towards it.
lessons.test: Headless scenario per scene type, run fast with --fixed-fps: time until ready for departure at 60, 150, 400 and 650 m, plus a run with followers forced close to prove the watchdog.

lessons.title: Performance.TIME_PROCESS is the slowest whole frame of the last second, not your scripts' time
lessons.symptom: A frame log labelled process and physics time as averages: they stayed high for a second after one slow frame and did not add up to the frame times. An automatic trigger that started profiling when this value was high found no slow script, because the frames were waiting for the GPU.
lessons.cause: Godot measures the whole main-loop frame (scripts, engine work, the render submit and any wait for the GPU), keeps the largest value of each second, and publishes it once per second through Performance.TIME_PROCESS; TIME_PHYSICS_PROCESS works the same way for physics steps.
lessons.fix: Label these monitors as the maximum per second. For per-frame values and for script time, time the phases yourself with Time.get_ticks_usec() (in an early and a late _process, set with process_priority, and around the physics steps), and trigger on those numbers.
lessons.test: Force one 50 ms frame: the monitor shows about 50 ms for up to a second afterwards. Make the GPU the bottleneck with light scripts and check that a script-time trigger stays off.

lessons.title: Detail smaller than a pixel at play distance turns into stripes; paint only what reads on screen
lessons.symptom: A large drone's fuselage showed streaks along its whole length in renders.
lessons.cause: Its colour and normal maps had 64 lengthwise seam lines (one every 22 cm) and about 16,000 rivets that were smaller than a pixel at normal viewing distance; filtering and lighting turned them into stripes. Strong contrast between top and bottom paint made the edge between them saw-toothed.
