lessons.fix: Keep only seams that match real panel breaks (a few ring and lengthwise seams), drop sub-pixel rivets, make seams wide enough to read at screen distance, soften the normal map (scale around 0.5) and lower the paint contrast. In procedural facade shaders, fade small repeating patterns such as windows to their average colour with distance.
lessons.test: Render at typical play distance before and after; no streaks or shimmer when the camera moves.

lessons.title: To place objects on a pattern a shader draws, replicate its hash in float32 on the CPU
lessons.symptom: Crops, pollard willows and hedgerows placed by script had to sit exactly on the field parcels and ditches that the terrain shader draws procedurally.
lessons.cause: GDScript floats are 64-bit, while the GPU evaluates fract()-based hashes in 32-bit floats. The same formula in GDScript gives different hash values, so parcels, ditches and rows land in different places.
lessons.fix: Port the shader's hash and noise line by line and round every intermediate result to 32 bits (for example through a one-element PackedFloat32Array), then use those values for placement.
lessons.test: Compare the GDScript port with a float32 reference (for example numpy) over many points, then check in a render that the objects line up with the drawn ditches.

lessons.title: Work done once per physics tick doubles when the tick rate doubles; tie substeps to time
lessons.symptom: After moving to 120 physics ticks per second a ship-motion prediction cost twice as much as at 60, about 2 ms per tick per ship.
lessons.cause: The prediction advanced one substep per _physics_process call, so its cost followed physics_ticks_per_second instead of game time, and it ran for every ship.
lessons.fix: Advance substeps from an accumulator at a fixed rate in seconds (for example 60 per second) whatever the tick rate, run the prediction only for the ship the player is near, and update far ships at a lower rate by accumulating delta into one larger step.
lessons.test: Measure the script's cost per second at 60 and 120 ticks per second; it should stay the same.

lessons.title: Let exactly one handler own the escape key, and restore mouse capture only when no panel wants a cursor
lessons.symptom: With a weapon planner open, the escape key opened the pause menu instead of closing the planner; resuming then captured the mouse while the planner was still open, so there was no cursor and the console seemed frozen. In another mode a ship controller swallowed the key and the pause menu never opened.
lessons.cause: Several nodes handled the escape key in _input() or _unhandled_input(). Input reaches nodes in reverse tree order and the first one that marks it handled wins, so which UI reacted depended on tree order. The pause menu set Input.mouse_mode to MOUSE_MODE_CAPTURED on resume without checking what was still open.
lessons.fix: Add one small guard node as the last child of the root (it receives _input first) that closes the top-most open panel or camera and calls set_input_as_handled(); let vehicle and mode controllers ignore that key; when a menu closes, choose the mouse mode from what is still open, and let panels show the cursor again if something captured it.
lessons.test: A scripted input test: the key closes the open panel without opening the pause menu, the pause menu works afterwards, and the cursor is visible whenever a panel is open.

lessons.title: A mode that hides every CanvasLayer also hides global UI it does not own
lessons.symptom: The minimap disappeared in jets, trains, drones and on the ferry, in every mode that brings its own HUD.
lessons.cause: Those modes hid the old HUD by looping over the root's children and setting visible = false on every CanvasLayer, which also hit the global minimap layer. A height limit for the minimap below the cruise height of some aircraft hid it as well.
lessons.fix: Hide only your own layers, tracked by reference or by group. As a safety net, a global layer can set itself visible again each frame (it processes last under the root) and a watchdog can recreate it when it was freed.
lessons.test: Enter each mode in a test and assert that the global layer exists and is visible.

lessons.title: Instrument and autopilot signs must follow the flight model's own attitude convention
lessons.symptom: On new glass-cockpit displays the attitude horizon moved the wrong way in pitch and roll; on a drone the wing-levelling hold had the wrong sign and tilted the aircraft further in turns.
lessons.cause: The flight model stored attitude with its own signs (positive pitch meant nose down, the visual rotation was the negative of the stored angle), and the display and hold code assumed the usual nose-up-positive convention.
lessons.fix: Read the convention from the code that applies the attitude to the visual, define named sign constants once, and use them in every instrument and autopilot.
lessons.test: Put the aircraft in a known attitude (nose up 10 degrees, right bank 20 degrees) in a test and assert the sign of every displayed value and of the hold's correction.

lessons.title: Every extra noise loop in a big terrain shader adds compile time; keep land-use branches cheap
lessons.symptom: After adding a new land-use type with five extra fbm noise calls, the terrain shader no longer compiled within 3 minutes on the software renderer of the test machine.
lessons.cause: Each fbm call inlines several octaves of noise, and an uber-shader with a branch per land-use type compiles all branches; compile time grows with every inlined loop, which players also feel as a long first-load or a hitch.
lessons.fix: Use one cheap value-noise call per new branch, reuse noise already computed for the pixel, or sample a small tiling noise texture instead of fbm loops; measure shader compile time after each change.
lessons.test: Time the first compile of the terrain material headless or on the slowest target before and after a change.

lessons.title: A node that marks every key as handled hides those keys from tools that read _input()
lessons.symptom: Two debug hotkeys worked on foot and in most vehicles, but did nothing while a few drone vehicles were active.
lessons.cause: The vehicle scripts called set_input_as_handled() at the end of their key handler for every key, also keys they did not use. Events travel up the tree from the last nodes to the first, and the debug tools sat earlier in the tree, so they never received the event.
lessons.fix: Mark an event handled only inside the branch that used it. Let global tools that must always work also poll Input.is_key_pressed() with a rising-edge check once per frame, and guard against a double start. Refuse rebinding gameplay actions to keys reserved for tools.
lessons.test: With Input.parse_input_event(), press the key while a node that swallows every key is in the tree; the tool must still start, and pressing again while it runs must not restart it.

lessons.title: Procedural audio clicks when parameters jump per frame or the generator buffer runs dry
lessons.symptom: A synthesized train sound ticked when a lever or the horn switched, and again whenever the frame rate dipped.
lessons.cause: Volume and pitch were set once per frame, so the waveform jumped at each change; the AudioStreamGenerator buffer was short and filled only a little each frame, so a slow frame let playback run out of samples, and the gap is heard as a tick.
lessons.fix: Move every parameter toward its target per sample with a small smoothing filter, give sounds attack and release envelopes, use a longer buffer_length, and each frame fill all get_frames_available() frames with push_buffer().
lessons.test: Render the generator output with one artificially long frame in the middle; there must be no run of silent samples and no sample-to-sample step larger than in steady play.

lessons.title: Cap a synthesized motor tone below about 1 kHz; a pitch that rises with speed becomes a whine
lessons.symptom: Players complained of a shrill squeal from a high-speed train at top speed.
lessons.cause: The motor tone was a pure sine whose pitch rose linearly with speed, plus an overtone at twice the pitch. At top speed this reached about 1.7 to 5 kHz, the range where hearing is most sensitive.
lessons.fix: Soft-limit the pitch (for example a base plus a range times tanh of speed), keep it under about 0.9 kHz, drop overtones above about 0.7 kHz, put a gentle low-pass near 3 kHz on the output, and lower the motor when wind and rolling noise take over.
lessons.test: Call the synthesis function headless at top speed and measure energy at the expected frequencies with a single-bin DFT; nothing strong should remain above about 1 kHz.

lessons.title: A sea surface at sea level also appears inside tunnels and cuttings below it
lessons.symptom: Water cut straight through rail tunnels, open cuttings and underground halls far inland, wherever they lay below sea level.
lessons.cause: The ocean was one surface around the camera at sea level that also existed under the land. Terrain normally hides it, but from inside a tunnel, a cutting or a hall below sea level the camera sees it.
lessons.fix: Mask the water: discard water fragments inside the footprint of tunnels, cuttings, halls and walkways where the ground above is dry land, or clip the water only inside the closed tunnel volume. Give wet cuttings a closed floor and walls. With many shapes, keep them in a data texture with a coarse cell index and test the cell's box first.
lessons.test: Render each tunnel mouth, cutting and hall from inside with the mask off and on, and check from the open sea that no water is missing.

lessons.title: Give a shader hundreds of shapes in a data texture with a grid index, not a fixed uniform array
lessons.symptom: Terrain openings for tunnel portals stopped working after the 64th; later portals stayed covered by terrain. Later the openings vanished again when another module swapped the terrain shader.
lessons.cause: The rectangles were a fixed-size uniform array, and every fragment looped over all of them. The openings were injected once into a shader that another script replaced later.
lessons.fix: Pack the shapes into an ImageTexture (Image.FORMAT_RGBAF, two texels per shape) and add an index texture with the start and count per grid cell (Image.FORMAT_RGF). Read both with nearest filtering and integer texel reads, so a fragment tests only the shapes of its own cell. If you inject code into a shader you do not own, remember the shader's get_instance_id() and apply the code again when it changes, carrying the uniform values over.
lessons.test: Add more shapes than the old limit and check that each one cuts the terrain; swap the terrain shader at runtime and check that the openings come back.

lessons.title: An interior built for double-sided materials shows holes when the new material culls back faces
lessons.symptom: After a material upgrade, underground station halls had black gaps; from inside you could see through walls and ceilings.
lessons.cause: The procedural hall geometry had been built for double-sided materials, with some faces pointing outward. The new materials kept the default cull_mode, so those faces were culled when seen from inside.
lessons.fix: Keep cull_mode = CULL_DISABLED on such materials, or build interior faces with inward normals. When you replace a material, copy the cull mode and transparency settings of the old one.
lessons.test: Render the interior from the eye position against a magenta background, with glass made opaque black; every magenta pixel is a hole.

lessons.title: Surfaces stacked a few millimetres apart flicker; keep layers at least about 2 cm apart
lessons.symptom: Floors in station halls flickered: tiles, painted lines and raised tactile studs fought with what lay under them.
lessons.cause: The tile floor sat 5 mm above the concrete and the studs 1 mm above the painted line. At normal viewing distances the depth buffer cannot tell them apart (z-fighting).
lessons.fix: Separate stacked layers by 2 cm or more (here 20, 30, 34 and 36 mm), cut the lower surface away under the upper one, or use a decal for thin markings.
lessons.test: Look along the floor at a grazing angle from 20 to 50 m while moving the camera slowly; nothing may shimmer.

lessons.title: Stream ahead of a fast camera, but choose the near detail from the real camera
lessons.symptom: From a train at about 100 m/s, trees popped in 100 to 260 m ahead. After loading was moved ahead, a band from 100 to 256 m had no trees at all.
lessons.cause: Cells were loaded in rings around the camera and were not ready when a fast camera reached them. After the loading centre was moved several seconds ahead, the mid-detail level also measured distance to that point, about 600 m ahead, so it was never built around the actual camera.
lessons.fix: Load the outer rings around a point 1.5 to 6 s ahead in the direction of travel (capped), and decide each detail level by the distance to the real camera. Let each instance cut off at an exact distance in the shader so neighbouring levels meet, use VISIBILITY_RANGE_FADE_SELF for whole-group switches, and lengthen visibility ranges of trackside objects along fast routes.
lessons.test: Move a camera at the top speed along the route and count frames in which a cell inside the near range is still unbuilt; it should be zero.

lessons.title: Turn slopes measured in UV space into world directions before bending a normal
lessons.symptom: On rivers, the ripples leaned the wrong way on segments that ran at an angle to the world axes.
lessons.cause: The river mesh had its UV coordinates along and across the flow, and the shader used the height slope in UV space as if it were the slope in world x and z.
lessons.fix: Work out the world direction of each UV axis from screen-space derivatives of the world position and the UV (or pass a tangent from the mesh), and build the gradient along those directions before you set the normal.
lessons.test: Rotate a straight water strip by 0, 45 and 90 degrees; the lighting of the ripples must rotate with it.

lessons.title: Fade small ripples by pixel size and keep reflected rays above the horizon
lessons.symptom: Water sparkled with noisy glitter in the distance and showed grey ovals close to the camera.
lessons.cause: Wave detail smaller than a pixel aliased into glitter. On steep wave flanks the reflected view ray pointed below the horizon and picked up the lower half of the sky.
lessons.fix: Measure the pixel footprint with fwidth() of the world position and fade each ripple octave out once it is smaller than a few pixels. When the reflected ray points below a small minimum elevation, tilt the normal so that it does not.
lessons.test: Compare captures at 2, 200 and 2000 m from a low eye height, with and without the fade and the clamp.

lessons.title: Keep temporal history through small FOV changes; a speed zoom must not reset it every frame
lessons.symptom: Volumetric clouds looked fuzzy and blocky in the game, while a still camera showed them sharp.
lessons.cause: The clouds were traced for one in sixteen pixels per frame and built up over the following frames. The history was thrown away whenever the field of view changed by more than 0.05 degrees, and a speed-dependent zoom changed the FOV every frame.
lessons.fix: Carry the history over by reprojecting it with the new projection, and reset it only on a camera cut or a large FOV change (here more than 8 degrees); after a reset, avoid isolated speckles until the history has filled again.
lessons.test: Animate the FOV by plus or minus 0.3 degrees per frame and compare the image with a fixed FOV; they should match.

lessons.title: A full-screen quad needs bounds that never cull it and no automatic visibility range
lessons.symptom: All 3D clouds disappeared once the camera was more than about 7.6 km from the map centre or high in the sky.
lessons.cause: The clouds were drawn by a 2 m quad at the origin that the vertex shader stretches over the screen. A script that gives small objects a visibility range by their bounding box gave it a range measured from the origin.
lessons.fix: Give full-screen quads a huge custom_aabb or extra_cull_margin, and let automatic range or LOD tools skip any node that has a custom_aabb.
lessons.test: Teleport the camera 50 km from the origin and 20 km up; the effect must still draw.

lessons.title: Dynamic resolution must follow GPU time, not the frame rate
lessons.symptom: The picture got blurrier and stuttered while the frame rate did not improve.
lessons.cause: An adaptive scaler lowered scaling_3d_scale whenever the frame rate was below target. The game was limited by the CPU, so the scale dropped to 80 % without any gain, and each change of the scale rebuilds the render buffers, which itself causes a hitch.
lessons.fix: Measure the GPU time (RenderingServer.viewport_set_measure_render_time() and viewport_get_measured_render_time_gpu()) and scale only when the GPU is the limit. Change the scale rarely, in steps, with hysteresis, or fix it when the CPU is the bottleneck.
lessons.test: Make the scene CPU-heavy with the GPU idle; the scale must stay put.

lessons.title: An empty search result must not mean 'not searched yet', or the tree is searched every frame
lessons.symptom: A full-world test with a new aircraft ran at about 8.5 fps, and one cause found was a scene search that ran every frame; in another script, a node search every 2 s caused a regular hitch.
lessons.cause: A cache of UI layers used an empty array as its 'not filled yet' flag. In a world without such layers the search found nothing, so it searched the whole scene tree recursively every frame. Elsewhere find_child() over a scene of more than ten thousand nodes ran every 2 s even while the found node was still valid.
lessons.fix: Keep a separate boolean that records that the search ran, also when it found nothing. Cache found nodes and search again only when the cached node is no longer valid or has left the tree; better, let nodes register themselves or use a group.
lessons.test: Profile a scene where the search finds nothing; the search function must run once, not every frame.

lessons.title: A node that must work far from the player cannot live under a node that is streamed out
lessons.symptom: A distant target area never appeared when a missile arrived there, even though the missile and its camera were close to it.
lessons.cause: The node that builds that area on demand was a child of a local site node near the player's start. With the player and camera hundreds of kilometres away, that branch of the tree no longer ran, so its child stopped as well.
lessons.fix: Attach such services to the persistent world root, set process_mode to PROCESS_MODE_ALWAYS where needed, and trigger loading from every active camera and tracked projectile, not only from the player. A short log file of load decisions helps when the area does not appear.
lessons.test: Start far away, fire at the area and watch the remote camera; the area must load before impact.

lessons.title: Count a waypoint as passed once it is behind or beside the vehicle, not only when it is reached
lessons.symptom: On a plotted route, guided missiles circled a waypoint or crashed in sharp turns.
lessons.cause: The follower only moved on when it came within a radius of the waypoint. With a limited turn rate it could not get inside the radius in a sharp turn and kept orbiting.
lessons.fix: Also advance when the waypoint lies beside or behind the vehicle (the dot product of the heading and the direction to the waypoint falls below a threshold) or when the vehicle has crossed the plane through the waypoint at right angles to the route.
lessons.test: Fly routes with 90, 120 and 170 degree turns at full speed; the follower must never loop.

lessons.title: Exclude the owner from rays and projectiles that start inside or next to it
lessons.symptom: A missile exploded right after launch against a ship of its own group; a rotor downwash effect found its ground point on the aircraft's own fuselage.
lessons.cause: The impact and ground tests included the launching ship and its group, and the downwash ray started at the rotor hub inside the aircraft's own collider.
lessons.fix: Pass the owner's RID (and its group's) in the exclude list of the ray query, call add_collision_exception_with() for physical projectiles, and use only terrain and sea for a 'hit the ground' test.
lessons.test: Launch from a moving ship in tight formation and hover low over a deck; there must be no hit on the owner.

lessons.title: Find where a sight line meets a height field by stepping, then bisecting along the ray
lessons.symptom: Target markers placed by aiming at the terrain sat beside the line of sight, worst at shallow angles.
lessons.cause: The ray was stepped in 50 m steps and, at the first sample below the ground, the point was simply moved down to the terrain height, off the ray.
lessons.fix: Then halve the step between the last point above and the first point below the ground (about 12 halvings bring 50 m to about 1 cm) and keep the result on the ray. Return no hit for non-finite heights or a zero direction. Use shorter steps near the camera so narrow ridges are not skipped.
lessons.test: Check flat, sloped, out-of-range and grazing rays, also at large world coordinates; the hit must lie on the ray within a centimetre.

lessons.title: Plan an automatic stop with the slope over the whole braking distance
lessons.symptom: An automatic train stop overshot the station marker by more than 75 cm on a sloping approach, or had to use the emergency brake.
lessons.cause: The braking curve used the gradient under the train. Later downhill sections in the braking distance added energy that the plan did not expect.
lessons.fix: Sample the gradient along the remaining distance with the same smoothing window that the movement code uses, and plan with the most downhill value, or with the mean gradient from the height difference between here and the stop.
lessons.test: Run stops on flat, uphill, downhill and dip-then-rise profiles at 30, 60 and 120 fps; every stop must end within tolerance using only the service brake.

lessons.title: Route clicks to a SubViewport screen in 3D with the camera pose that was drawn
lessons.symptom: Clicks on cockpit screens missed their buttons, typed letters in a text field triggered game actions, and the tests passed in one setup and failed in another.
lessons.cause: Mouse positions were turned into screen pixels from the camera's physics pose instead of the interpolated pose on screen, event coordinates were not mapped between window and viewport scale, and key events were handled by the game while a text field had focus.
lessons.fix: Cast the ray with the camera used for drawing, intersect the screen mesh, convert the hit to SubViewport pixels, duplicate the event, set position, global_position and (for motion) relative, call notify_mouse_entered() or notify_mouse_exited(), and send it with push_input(event, true). Forward key events while gui_get_focus_owner() is a LineEdit, and always forward button releases so no press gets stuck.
lessons.test: Simulate real clicks with Input.parse_input_event() at 30, 60 and 120 fps while the vehicle moves.

lessons.title: In a headless test, simulated mouse motion is scaled by the window stretch
lessons.symptom: Look-around tests turned the camera about 12.8 times too far per pixel; mouse steering checks failed only headless.
lessons.cause: The headless window was 100 by 100 pixels while the content scale size was 1280 by 720, so every simulated mouse event was stretched into the larger content space.
lessons.fix: Turn content_scale_mode off in the test (or size the window to the content), or compute the expected motion with the same stretch transform.
lessons.test: Send one motion event of 100 pixels and assert the camera turns by the angle the sensitivity setting gives.

lessons.title: Run per-instance selection loops on a worker thread and upload the result on the main thread
lessons.symptom: Along a forested route about six frames per second took 40 ms, 27 ms of it in one GDScript loop.
lessons.cause: Several times per second the main thread sorted up to three thousand nearby trees into detail groups and rebuilt the MultiMesh buffers.
lessons.fix: Snapshot the input arrays (PackedFloat32Array copies are copy-on-write) and run the loop with WorkerThreadPool.add_task(); poll is_task_completed() each frame and only write MultiMesh buffers on the main thread. Fill lazy caches before you start tasks, never call node functions such as get_meta() from a task, and pass plain Dictionary values. For a long parallel build, write a marker file first and fall back to the main thread on the next start if the marker is still there.
lessons.test: Compare the 99th percentile frame time along the route before and after, and compare a hash of the results of the threaded and single-thread builds.

lessons.title: Bake vertex ambient occlusion with a fixed ray set, spatial smoothing and opaque occluders only
lessons.symptom: Baked ambient occlusion in a train cab showed streaks across the desk; in an earlier try the desk turned black under the windscreen.
lessons.cause: Each vertex used a randomly rotated set of rays, so neighbouring vertices of large flat triangles got very different values; glass was counted as an occluder.
lessons.fix: Use one fixed ray set, start rays slightly off the surface along the normal, average the result over small cells (a few centimetres) of vertices with a similar normal, clamp to a minimum, and skip transparent and unshaded surfaces both as occluders and as targets.
lessons.test: Render close-ups of large flat panels before and after, and compare the mean AO with the previous bake.

lessons.title: Check UV area and tangents of normal-mapped meshes before export
lessons.symptom: Textures smeared over hundreds of faces of an aircraft skin, and export audits found missing and broken tangents on normal-mapped parts.
lessons.cause: Some faces had collapsed UV islands with zero area, n-gons got no tangents in the export, and some primitives had a broken tangent basis (non-unit or degenerate tangents).
lessons.fix: Measure the UV area of every face and re-project collapsed faces (for example planar on their dominant normal at a fixed texel density), triangulate before you export tangents, check that tangents have unit length and a sign of plus or minus one, and test the normal map's green channel (Godot expects Y+).
lessons.test: Run a script that reports faces with zero UV area and invalid tangents per primitive, and render a raised and a sunken detail to check the normal direction.

lessons.title: A polygon multiplier is not a quality target; budget triangles and make the game switch LODs
lessons.symptom: Requests for 'seven times more polygons' gave aircraft of 3.5 to over 50 million triangles at the top level, packs of gigabytes, and an evenly densified cockpit that added no real detail; in the game the vehicle always used its most detailed level.
lessons.cause: Even subdivision adds vertices on flat panels without changing silhouette or shading, and the exported lower levels were not used because the loader picked the high model and the switch was off by default.
lessons.fix: Set a triangle budget per view distance and spend it where silhouette, curvature and close-up views need it. Export lower levels and make sure they switch in the game (visibility_range_begin and visibility_range_end, or visibility_parent). Accept a model only after measuring frame time, memory and load time in the engine.
lessons.test: Count the triangles actually drawn at 10, 100 and 1000 m in the game, and measure memory before and after spawning the model.

lessons.title: Run overlap and area tests far from the origin in local coordinates
lessons.symptom: A placement check reported more than twice as many overlapping buildings as there really were.
lessons.cause: Areas and intersections were computed in 32-bit floats at tens of kilometres from the origin, and rounding noise looked like overlap.
lessons.fix: Subtract a local origin (such as the cell or object centre) before geometric tests, and use 64-bit floats for areas. In GDScript a float is 64-bit, but Vector2 and Vector3 are 32-bit in standard builds.
lessons.test: Move a known non-overlapping layout 50 km away from the origin and run the check; it must still report zero.

lessons.title: Saved settings need a migration when a default changes or a key becomes reserved
lessons.symptom: After actions moved off two function keys and the mouse pitch default flipped, players with an older settings file still had the old keys and the old direction.
lessons.cause: New defaults only apply to entries that are missing; a saved ConfigFile keeps the old values.
lessons.fix: Store a settings version; on load, move bindings off reserved keys to a free key, apply a changed default once, replace invalid values with the default, and still read older versions. Refuse rebinding to reserved keys with a message.
lessons.test: Load settings files from each earlier version and a broken one, and check the resulting bindings and values.

lessons.title: Unshaded smoke glows at night; tint it with the light of the scene
lessons.symptom: Smoke and dust clouds from missile launches glowed brightly at night.
lessons.cause: The smoke used an unshaded material with a fixed colour, which ignores lighting.
lessons.fix: Multiply the smoke colour by the current sun and ambient light (for example from a global shader parameter set by the day cycle), or use a lit material with soft normals; keep only flames and flashes emissive.
lessons.test: Capture the same effect at noon, dusk and night; the smoke must darken with the scene while the flame does not.

lessons.title: Project HUD symbols only for points in front of the camera's near plane
lessons.symptom: A helmet display spammed engine errors when the horizon line was drawn about 90 degrees to the side.
lessons.cause: Camera3D.unproject_position() was called for points on or behind the camera plane, where the projection divides by zero.
lessons.fix: Transform the point into camera space and skip it when its depth is less than the near distance, or test is_position_behind() first; clip lines against the near plane instead of projecting both ends.
lessons.test: Turn the view 90 and 180 degrees from the symbol and check that no errors are printed.

lessons.title: Clamp an orbit or chase camera to the space it is in: above the ground, inside the tube
lessons.symptom: An orbit camera around a parked aircraft dropped about 4 m under the ground; a chase camera left a transit tube and a station roof.
lessons.cause: The orbit code limited only the angle and distance, not where the camera ended up.
lessons.fix: After computing the orbit pose, clamp it: at least a little above the vehicle's ground line and the terrain, inside tunnels and halls, and above water unless the view is meant to be submerged; move the camera closer rather than through the wall.
lessons.test: Orbit through all angles with the vehicle parked, in a tunnel and on a deck, and check the camera height and that the view is not blocked.

lessons.title: Parts pinned to an interpolated node must be interpolated too, or they drift apart in motion
lessons.symptom: In flight the side structure of a cockpit slid about 120 px (roughly 6 degrees) against the instrument panel and the outside shell: terrain showed through the gap, beams floated in view and an edge was doubled. Standing still everything lined up, and every transform the scripts read agreed within half a millimetre.
lessons.cause: With physics interpolation on, a node is drawn between its last two physics poses. The outside shell inherited interpolation ON, while the cockpit subtree had it OFF through an ancestor, and a script copied the shell's global_transform onto the cockpit every frame. That copy is the raw tick pose, so on screen one half was interpolated and the other was not. global_transform never shows the difference, which is why no CPU-side measurement could see it.
lessons.fix: Keep everything that must look rigid in one interpolation regime: parent the parts under one node instead of copying transforms, and give the whole assembly the same physics_interpolation_mode. If a pose must be copied in _process, copy get_global_transform_interpolated() and turn interpolation off on the copy. Decide separately for effects (rotor wash, exhaust) that hang on the same body, so they do not trail behind.
lessons.test: Dump is_physics_interpolated_and_enabled() for every node of the assembly and require one value per rigid group; compare a still frame with a frame at speed from the same camera and count changed pixels on the structure (here 11 percent before, about 1 percent after).

lessons.title: Move a moving platform on every physics tick, not on every second one
lessons.symptom: A helicopter parked on a ship sailing at 40 knots slid more than 2 m across the deck; the test measured the deck jumping up to 0.84 m between ticks.
lessons.cause: The ship's motion clock advanced on every second physics tick, so at 30 Hz while physics ran at 60 Hz. The deck collider teleported about 0.69 m per update plus the heave, and stood still on the tick in between. A CharacterBody3D or a contact solver cannot follow a floor that jumps on alternate ticks, so the body lost the floor and slid.
lessons.fix: Advance the platform in _physics_process on every tick (for example an AnimatableBody3D moved there), or interpolate its pose between slower clock updates. Test fixtures that drive the platform must also step every physics frame, or they test a different motion than the game.
lessons.test: Record the platform's displacement per tick: it should be about speed divided by the tick rate on every tick, with no alternating zero steps. Measure the drift of a parked body over 20 s or more at top speed and in heavy sea.

lessons.title: A contact delay before attaching to a moving deck becomes a permanent offset
lessons.symptom: A check that a parked helicopter stays in place on a moving deck failed by about 11 cm with clean logs, although the carrying itself moved less than 4 mm per tick.
lessons.cause: The carry code waited for two consecutive contact ticks before attaching. During the first, unattached tick the deck moved 5 cm and the body did not; the rigid delta carry then held that offset for as long as it carried. The test measured the attach delay, not the rigidity.
lessons.fix: Attach on the first contact, or attach a body that is spawned on the deck right away with the deck's velocity. In tests, measure the spread of the offset after attaching separately from the transient while attaching.
lessons.test: Spawn on a deck that moves several centimetres per tick: with the contact counter pre-set the drift fell from about 0.11 m to 0.02 m in the same run.

lessons.title: Release a body locked to a moving deck as soon as the deck data turns invalid
lessons.symptom: With a deck record that was present but invalid (an empty outline polygon), a parked helicopter stayed locked and kept being carried with nonsense data instead of being released.
lessons.cause: The validity check tested the record's fields but not its polygon, and the inside-the-outline test only guarded a new lock. An existing lock therefore survived an empty polygon, and the tests only covered acquiring a lock.
lessons.fix: Validate the whole record on every tick (at least three outline points, finite velocity, the expected frame of reference) and release within one frame when it fails, keeping the last valid deck velocity so the body does not jump. Add a regression test that corrupts the record after the lock.
lessons.test: Lock onto a deck, then empty its outline: the body must be released within a tick and keep its velocity.

lessons.title: A path check must use the moving body's own shape, margin and obstacles
lessons.symptom: Two crew members walking to a vehicle stopped at a door and re-planned every two seconds for minutes: the planner said the way was free while move_and_slide() kept refusing it. Elsewhere eleven walking routes were blocked by door leaves that stood fully open.
lessons.cause: The planner's shape cast used a 5 mm margin while the CharacterBody3D moved with a safe_margin of 15 mm, and the planner's obstacle list left out opened door panels that physics did collide with. The planner and physics disagreed, so the same blocked route was chosen again and again.
lessons.fix: Plan with the same shape, the same margin (the shape query's margin equal to the body's safe_margin) and the same colliders as the body, including animated doors in their open pose. Log when the planner accepts a step but the body makes no progress, and count that as a failure.
lessons.test: Run every route with real physics bodies and doors open and closed; a route the planner accepts must be walkable.

lessons.title: Detect a stuck agent by lack of progress toward its goal, and give every wait a limit
lessons.symptom: Two NPCs waited forever behind a door, so the mission could not continue; a test of it ended only on the runner's time-out after 145 s, with no error in the log.
lessons.cause: The follow function returned false until arrival, nothing counted how long that lasted, and the only recovery paths needed a state that the stuck crew prevented. A detector on 'not moving' would never fire either, because the capsules slid along the door leaf and swung between waypoints.
lessons.fix: Track whether the flat distance to the goal shrinks by a minimum amount within a time window; when it does not, escalate: re-plan around the blocked zone, try another entrance, or fall back to a defined state with a message to the player. Do not count false returns of a function that is false on every normal step, and do not fix it by raising wait times.
lessons.test: Reproduce the blocking obstacle in a test that requires the agents to really arrive, plus a case where an agent slides sideways at equal distance from its goal.

lessons.title: Hiding a node hides its children but does not stop their input, picking or collisions
lessons.symptom: A hidden cockpit interior kept taking clicks: a ray from the mouse switched on an invisible battery switch, and keyboard and gamepad navigation moved through hidden controls. In another case, hiding a building's body made every detail batch and sign parented under it disappear.
lessons.cause: visible only affects drawing, and children inherit it. Scripts keep processing, CollisionObject3D shapes stay in the physics space and stay ray-pickable, and focus can still land on hidden controls.
lessons.fix: To switch something off, set process_mode to PROCESS_MODE_DISABLED (collision objects with the default disable_mode leave the physics space) or turn off its input handling, collision shapes and input_ray_pickable explicitly, and release focus. Parent detail that must stay visible outside the node you hide.
lessons.test: After switching a panel off, cast the same screen ray, press the same keys and assert that no control changed state.

lessons.title: Set metadata and properties before add_child() when the node reads them in _ready()
lessons.symptom: A probe meant to measure the start on a ship silently measured the normal start: the flags that chose the ship route were there afterwards, but the consumer had already decided.
lessons.cause: add_child() runs _enter_tree() and _ready() of the new subtree right away. Metadata set on the line after add_child() arrives after _ready() has already read it.
lessons.fix: Configure an instanced scene (set_meta(), exported properties) before add_child(), or let the consumer read the value later, through a deferred call or a signal.
lessons.test: Assert inside the consumer's _ready() that the expected flag is present.

lessons.title: Find the nodes you generate by metadata or class, not by name
lessons.symptom: A duplicate check missed eleven of twelve generated sections; a search for a panel matched a fitting the same tool had added earlier, giving a negative width; a name filter for particle emitters also caught an audio player with the same name.
lessons.cause: When a sibling already has the name, add_child() gives the new node a generated variant of the name, so exact-name checks miss copies. Substring matches also hit unrelated nodes, including ones your own code added on an earlier run.
lessons.fix: Mark nodes you create with set_meta() or put them in a group and query by that; filter by class (node is GPUParticles3D) as well as by name; skip nodes that carry your own marker when you search the original model.
lessons.test: Run the generator twice on the same scene: node counts must not change and nothing may be added twice.

lessons.title: Read an anchor's pose relative to the node you attach to, not its position property
lessons.symptom: A demister strip added to a cockpit hung as a loose bar across the view through the windscreen instead of lying on the glare shield, about 20 cm too high and too far forward.
lessons.cause: The code read the anchor's position, which is relative to its own parent. Earlier anchors were direct children of the cockpit root, so it had worked, but this one sat inside an intermediate group.
lessons.fix: Compute the pose in the frame you attach to: root.global_transform.affine_inverse() * anchor.global_transform, or multiply the local transforms up the chain. If the anchor is missing, add nothing rather than a part at a guessed place.
lessons.test: Assert the distance from the added part to its anchor surface, measured in the root's frame.

lessons.title: Local coordinates under a scaled node are not metres
lessons.symptom: A probe that put sample points on a windscreen found almost nothing: its heights were off by a factor of 0.8 and a pivot by a factor of 1.84, and a shape comparison made in that frame was invalid.
lessons.cause: The cockpit root had a non-uniform scale. Positions converted with its inverse transform (to_local()) come out in that node's scaled units, while the targets were given in metres.
lessons.fix: Convert explicitly: divide by the node's scale, or measure in an unscaled frame. Avoid non-uniform scale on nodes that have rotated children or that other code measures against.
lessons.test: Send a known offset in metres through to_local() and back and compare its length with the expected value.

lessons.title: Compare a measured jitter with the float32 step before calling it motion
lessons.symptom: An eye-to-cockpit wobble of about 1.2 mm per frame was reported as a proven oscillation and later withdrawn; a related camera test kept flipping on a 5 mm limit.
lessons.cause: About 7 km from the origin a 32-bit float has a step of 0.49 mm. The non-zero steps took only a handful of distinct values, all exact multiples of that step: a quantisation lattice, not movement. The relative pose had been computed by subtracting large global positions.
lessons.fix: Compare any sub-millimetre measurement with the float32 step at that position. Compute relative poses from the local transform chain (a step of about 0.0001 mm there) instead of from differences of global transforms, and put test thresholds well above the noise floor.
lessons.test: Make a histogram of the measured steps: a few repeating values at multiples of the float step mean quantisation.

lessons.title: Give every transform one writer per frame
lessons.symptom: A cockpit kept a small wobble against the eye point, and a pose offset that one script added in _physics_process never showed on screen.
lessons.cause: The camera and the cockpit were placed by two independent scripts. A sync function was called at least twice per frame from several places, and a later sync in _process overwrote what another script had set in _physics_process. The last writer silently wins.
lessons.fix: Let one owner write each node's transform once per frame and have other systems pass offsets to it. Parent the camera under what it must stay rigid to. When a function is reachable from several paths, guard it with a frame counter.
lessons.test: In a debug build count writes to the transform per frame and log which script made the final one.

lessons.title: Moving a cockpit mesh must move its pick shapes, screens and support parts too
lessons.symptom: Moving a cockpit core up by 25 cm would have left every clickable button a quarter of a metre below its picture; pedal supports stayed behind when the pedal group moved.
lessons.cause: The fit was checked in the modelling file, which has no Area3D, CollisionShape3D or SubViewport screens, so a passing geometry check proved nothing about the controls. Pick areas, display quads and supports were siblings that do not follow the mesh.
lessons.fix: Keep each control's mesh, pick shape and screen under one parent that moves together, and add a check that every pick shape and screen still sits on its control within a small tolerance (1.5 mm here).
lessons.test: For every interactive control compare the centre of its pick shape with its mesh in the cockpit frame, including a case where a sibling is deliberately left behind.

lessons.title: Where the model touches the ground must be where its collider touches
lessons.symptom: A helicopter's skids hovered 25 cm above the deck: the visible skids ended 1.50 m below the origin, the collider 1.75 m. A motorcycle rider's helmet stuck 10 cm out of the obstacle box.
lessons.cause: Visual model and collision shapes came from different sources and were never compared. The obstacle box was a constant per vehicle class, and the new model was taller.
lessons.fix: Derive collision extents from the actual mesh or check them against it: the lowest visible contact point equals the collider's bottom, and the collider covers the visual envelope. Repeat the check after every model swap.
lessons.test: In a headless test compute both from the loaded scene and assert they differ by less than a centimetre.

lessons.title: A bounding box is not a measurement
lessons.symptom: Bounding boxes misled the team three times: a rotor hub's box was taken as its position, an asymmetric rim was measured instead of the tyre, and a box test claimed a part sat behind the windscreen when it did not.
lessons.cause: An AABB is aligned to the axes and includes everything in the node, so rotated parts, flanges and hollow shells inflate it. Overlapping boxes are weak evidence; only a box that is entirely outside a volume proves something.
lessons.fix: Measure on the real geometry: node origins for pivots, ray hits on triangles (Geometry3D.ray_intersects_triangle()) for surfaces, and the specific mesh (the tyre, not the wheel) for sizes.
lessons.test: Check one known dimension of the part with your method before trusting the rest of its numbers.

lessons.title: Check that details are not buried inside a solid, not only that they do not stick out
lessons.symptom: The glass and glazing bars of bay windows were invisible, hidden inside the masonry, while the geometry validator reported zero problems.
lessons.cause: The validator only flagged parts that protruded from their volume. An earlier fix for protrusion pushed the glass inward, and the validator kept steering that way.
lessons.fix: Bracket each detail from both sides: its face must lie in a thin band just outside the surface it belongs to (inside means hidden, far outside means floating). Add a regression check that feeds the old broken values and must report them.
lessons.test: The regression check flags every known-bad case and stays quiet on the good ones.

lessons.title: Generated triangles must be clockwise seen from the front, or the surface is lit from below
lessons.symptom: A generated dune surface rendered dull and far darker than its vertex colours, and could vanish from some angles.
lessons.cause: The triangles were wound counter-clockwise as seen from above. Godot treats clockwise winding as the front face, so the generated normals pointed down (mean normal y of minus 0.98): the mesh got no sunlight, only ambient light, and back-face culling could hide it.
lessons.fix: Emit indices clockwise as seen from the visible side (or swap two indices per triangle) before generating normals, and for terrain-like meshes assert that the mean normal points up.
lessons.test: Mean normal y of a ground mesh greater than zero; sample the rendered colour against the vertex colour at a few points.

lessons.title: Rebuilding an imported mesh surface from its arrays re-encodes every vertex
lessons.symptom: Finishing passes on imported cockpit meshes failed their own guard with 'original attribute changed' for position, normal, tangent and UV; in another pass the edited normals and tangents came back unchanged.
lessons.cause: Imported meshes keep normals and tangents packed into the vertex buffer and, with attribute compression, store positions and texture coordinates quantised as well. surface_get_arrays() decodes them and add_surface_from_arrays() encodes them again, so every vertex can move a little. Code that treats them as plain arrays does not touch the packed data.
lessons.fix: Leave the original vertex buffers alone: change only index arrays (move triangles to a new surface or drop them), or add your finishing as a separate surface or mesh. Compare the buffers byte for byte after the edit.
lessons.test: After the edit the vertex data of untouched surfaces is byte-identical to the import.

lessons.title: A BoxMesh is not an ArrayMesh: guard calls that only ArrayMesh has
lessons.symptom: An export script failed with a nonexistent-function error on box-shaped parts: their rows were never written, the data files written just before were left orphaned, and the run still reported passed.
lessons.cause: surface_get_primitive_type() and similar surface queries exist on ArrayMesh, not on PrimitiveMesh classes such as BoxMesh. The call failed after the data files had been written, and the error ended the function.
lessons.fix: Check mesh is ArrayMesh before ArrayMesh-only calls and default to Mesh.PRIMITIVE_TRIANGLES for primitive meshes (their surface_get_arrays() works). Write output files only once the record is complete, and let log errors fail the test.
lessons.test: Run the exporter on a scene with both a BoxMesh and an imported mesh and require a complete record for each.

lessons.title: Know which material slot wins before you recolour or coat part of a mesh
lessons.symptom: A coating applied to small fittings did nothing; a recolour with an overlay left the old yellow showing; a fix aimed at the rotor left a yellow band that actually came from another surface of a static body mesh.
lessons.cause: GeometryInstance3D.material_override replaces every surface and beats per-surface overrides, so a helper that had set it blocked the coating. material_overlay only draws an extra pass on top. And the colour came from a shared atlas on a different surface than the node that was assumed.
lessons.fix: Trace a wrong pixel to its triangle and surface first. Change the colour with set_surface_override_material() on exactly that surface, clear a material_override that a helper set, and store the previous material so the change can be undone.
lessons.test: Render again, sample the same pixel, and check that the restore path puts the original material back.

lessons.title: A reparented branch is caught by every helper that walks its new parent
lessons.symptom: After the exterior model was moved under the cockpit node to keep the two aligned, it changed render layer, lost its shadows after a view switch, and could no longer be culled on its own.
lessons.cause: Helpers that set render layers and that switch off shadows for performance walked the cockpit subtree recursively, and now walked the exterior too. It moved from layer 20 to the cockpit's layer 19, which camera cull masks, a picture-in-picture view and light cull masks rely on.
lessons.fix: Treat a reparented branch as a guest: mark it, skip it in recursive helpers, and restore its layers and cast_shadow after any such pass. Remember that layer number n in set_layer_mask_value() and set_cull_mask_value() is bit value 2 to the power n minus 1 when you compare dumps.
lessons.test: After every view or mode switch assert that the guest branch's layers and cast_shadow equal the values recorded when it was attached.

lessons.title: Write transforms, shader parameters and environment values only when they change
lessons.symptom: Per-script profiling found many small per-frame costs: 0.4 ms for warning lights rewriting their material, 0.38 ms for a HUD rewriting its text and position, 1 ms for weapon mounts on distant ships writing unchanged transforms, five environment writes per frame, and a wind value uploaded to 30 materials 120 times a second.
lessons.cause: Property setters such as set_shader_parameter(), Environment properties and node transforms do their work (rendering server calls, transform notifications) even when the value is the same, and these ran every frame or every physics tick.
lessons.fix: Keep the last written value and write only on change; slow down what the player cannot see change (10 Hz far from the camera, a few times per second for hidden banners); use one shared material or a global shader parameter for values such as wind.
lessons.test: Measure _process time per script before and after; behaviour must stay identical.

lessons.title: The water shader and the code that samples water height must share one formula
lessons.symptom: The boat code and the landing checks used a water height up to 0.28 m away from the waves on screen; a proposed detail upgrade also used a normal that was not the slope of its own wave.
lessons.cause: The vertex shader and the CPU sampler each had their own copy of the wave sum with different defaults and mesh scale, and they drifted apart; the new normal was made by hand instead of derived.
lessons.fix: Keep the wave parameters in one place and evaluate the same function on the CPU and in the shader, fed from the same values; derive the normal analytically from that function; cut off waves that are shorter than a ring of the water mesh can show.
lessons.test: Sample the CPU height and the shader height on a grid of points and require agreement within a few millimetres.

lessons.title: Decide 'underwater' from the water itself, not from the camera being below sea level
lessons.symptom: In a closed tunnel under the sea the underwater effect, fog and muffled sound switched on.
lessons.cause: The underwater passes were keyed only on the camera's height being below the global sea level, which is also true in dry tunnels, cellars and land below sea level.
lessons.fix: Test for actual water: the sea mask or water area at that point, and not inside an enclosed dry volume such as an Area3D around a tunnel. Keep real sea cameras on the underwater path.
lessons.test: Drive through the tunnel and dive below the surface; only the second may switch the effect on.

lessons.title: A clipped Label cuts through a letter unless you set an overrun behaviour
lessons.symptom: A panel title was cut off in the middle of a letter, while the line of text below it ended neatly with an ellipsis.
lessons.cause: Both labels had clip_text on, but the title kept text_overrun_behavior at OVERRUN_NO_TRIMMING while the line below used an ellipsis mode.
lessons.fix: For text that may not fit, set text_overrun_behavior to OVERRUN_TRIM_WORD_ELLIPSIS, or wrap to a fixed number of lines with autowrap_mode and max_lines_visible. Test with the longest real strings at the smallest supported resolution.
lessons.test: Render the panel with its longest title at 720p and check that no glyph is cut.

lessons.title: Reserve fixed space for changing HUD text so the layout does not jump
lessons.symptom: Every time a status line switched between one and three lines the whole HUD card moved: twelve layout changes for twelve status changes, seen as HUD stutter.
lessons.cause: A wrapping Label changes its height with its line count, and the container laid the card out again on every change.
lessons.fix: Give dynamic text a fixed capacity, with custom_minimum_size or a fixed number of lines (max_lines_visible), and anchors that do not depend on text length; update only the text.
lessons.test: Cycle through all status messages and assert that the card's global rectangle stays the same.

lessons.title: Keep a camera's base value apart from the effects you add on top
lessons.symptom: In a train cab the mouse wheel zoomed out on every click, forward or back, once the train was fast.
lessons.cause: A speed effect added up to 9 degrees to Camera3D.fov. The zoom code read the current fov, including that push, as its new base, so each click stored a wider base.
lessons.fix: Store the base value yourself and compose fov = base + effects every frame; input changes only the base. The same holds for shake offsets and look offsets on positions.
lessons.test: At speed, one click in followed by one click out must return to the same base value.

lessons.title: A Timer started before its node is in the tree never runs
lessons.symptom: The smoke marker at a landing zone never appeared when the layer that owned it was created before it was added to the scene.
lessons.cause: Timer.start() fails when the timer is not inside the scene tree, and the timer was started while its layer was not yet in the tree.
lessons.fix: Set autostart before the timer enters the tree, start it in _ready(), or use get_tree().create_timer() once the node is in the tree.
lessons.test: Build the layer outside the tree, add it later, and assert that the timeout fires.
errors: Unable to start the timer because it's not inside the scene tree

lessons.title: Give automated Godot runs their own user data folder
lessons.symptom: Test runs started next to the player's running game logged a renderer cache error and risked overwriting the player's settings and saves.
lessons.cause: Every run of the same project shares the user data folder and the shader cache in the user's profile, so parallel test runs and the real game read and write the same files.
lessons.fix: Point each test run at its own profile before Godot starts (on Windows set the application data environment variables for the child process, or use a test copy with application/config/use_custom_user_dir), and hash the player's saves before and after a run.
lessons.test: Run a test while the game is open; the player's files must be byte-identical afterwards and the log free of cache errors.

lessons.title: Give scenario tests a budget in simulated time, plus a separate wall-clock watchdog
lessons.symptom: A world test on the installed game was aborted by its 180 s deadline while a train was still braking towards the platform.
lessons.cause: The deadline was wall-clock time, but the scenario needs a fixed amount of physics time; on a slower machine or with a heavy load the same scenario takes longer.
lessons.fix: Express how long a scenario may take in physics frames or simulated seconds, keep a generous wall-clock watchdog only for hangs, and report which of the two ended the run.
lessons.test: Run the scenario with a reduced Engine.max_fps or on a slow machine: it must still pass or fail on its own criteria.

lessons.title: Measure the run-to-run spread of tail frame times before you gate on them
lessons.symptom: Performance gates of 3 percent on the 99th percentile frame time and a fixed limit on the 95th failed and passed on the same build; one verdict came down to 0.04 ms. A functional gate flipped the same way on a 3.5 mm margin.
lessons.cause: Over repeated 10 s runs the mean frame time varied 1.5 percent while the 95th percentile varied 16 percent and the 99th 32 percent; a few runs never got up to speed (under a hundred frames) and their numbers meant nothing. Tail statistics of short samples are decided by a handful of frames.
lessons.fix: Warm up first (about 30 s), sample a fixed long window (60 s), discard runs that never reached a steady state, rerun the same build to measure its spread, and only call a change a regression when it is larger than that spread. Do not set fixed thresholds right at the value a build sits on.
lessons.test: Run the unchanged build five times and record the spread of every gated number next to its threshold.

lessons.title: A load that never yields freezes the loading screen and makes the OS call the game unresponsive
lessons.symptom: The loading screen stayed at 0 percent and the window showed that the program was not responding; the longest gap without a processed frame was 45 s.
lessons.cause: The cockpit and the world were built synchronously on the main thread (12 s and 19 s), including 5.5 s of parsing raw glTF files. No frame ran, so the loading screen could not redraw and the window stopped answering the OS. Threaded ResourceLoader requests did not help, because raw .glb files packed without import are not resources it can load.
lessons.fix: Split the build into steps that await a frame in between; parse raw glTF with GLTFDocument.append_from_buffer() on a Thread and call generate_scene() on the main thread (under 10 ms here); let loading be cancelled and wait for all worker threads before quitting.
lessons.test: Log the longest gap between processed frames during loading; for the glTF part it fell from 5.5 s to 39 ms.

lessons.title: Large textures imported as lossless sit uncompressed in video memory
lessons.symptom: Textures took about 7 GB of video memory and distant surfaces shimmered.
lessons.cause: Hundreds of 2K and 4K textures were imported in lossless mode without mipmaps. That mode only shrinks the file: on the GPU every texel is full RGBA8, and without mipmaps distant surfaces alias.
lessons.fix: Import textures used in 3D as VRAM compressed with mipmaps: colour maps as BC1 or BC3, normal maps with the normal map option (RGTC). Godot picks the two-channel BC5 format by itself when the blue channel is zero everywhere, which also suits packed occlusion-roughness maps without a metal channel. Expect four to eight times less memory.
lessons.test: Load a sample of textures from the exported pack and check their format and mipmap count; compare video memory before and after.

lessons.title: Check generated textures for content, not only that they import and load
lessons.symptom: A batch of generated normal maps loaded without errors but added no surface detail, and decals showed banding along their edges when enlarged.
lessons.cause: The normal maps had very few unique colours, almost no spread in red and green and a constant blue channel, so they were effectively flat. The decal masks had about eleven alpha levels instead of 256. Import and load checks cannot see either problem.
lessons.fix: Add a content check per texture type: normal maps need spread in red and green and a varying blue channel; judge decals on their alpha channel; allow constant packed material maps; keep hard failures apart from warnings. Measure at full resolution, not on a thumbnail.
lessons.test: Feed the check a known flat normal map and a known good one; only the first may fail.

lessons.title: Shape terrain profiles with smoothstep, not pow() with an exponent below one
lessons.symptom: Generated dunes had a sharp step of up to 0.5 m where they met the beach and the valley behind them.
lessons.cause: pow(x, e) with e below one has an infinite slope at x = 0, so the profile jumps right where it meets flat ground.
lessons.fix: Shape transitions with smoothstep(), which has zero slope at both ends, or with an exponent above one; check the slopes of generated profiles as well as their heights (a slope steeper than sand can hold also needed a wider base).
lessons.test: Sample the profile's slope at both ends and assert it stays under the material's angle of repose.

lessons.title: Deferred calls from physics callbacks run inside the physics step, where profilers count them as physics
lessons.symptom: A frame profiler blamed the physics server for spikes of 0.3 to 0.5 s, with 18 ms per physics step for seconds at a time, although no area signals were connected and few bodies were active.
lessons.cause: Godot flushes the deferred-call queue during every physics iteration, after _physics_process and again after the physics server step. Everything queued with call_deferred() from a physics callback runs in that gap, including nodes added with add_child.call_deferred() and their _ready(). A timer from the end of the physics scripts to the next frame therefore counts that building work as physics.
lessons.fix: Split the gap: queue a marker with call_deferred() right after the last _physics_process of the step and time from there. Report the deferred part on its own, with the number of new nodes and the scripts that made them, and then spread that building work over frames.
lessons.test: In a test scene, add about a hundred nodes per physics tick from a physics callback and check that the profiler reports the time as deferred work, not as physics.

lessons.title: current_scene does not contain the nodes that live beside it under the root
lessons.symptom: Effects on several aircraft looked for the sun, never found it, and searched again every second over the whole scene at 7 to 28 ms per search.
lessons.cause: The sun belonged to a persistent node placed directly under the root window, next to the current scene. get_tree().current_scene.find_children() only searches the current scene's branch, so nodes from autoloads or other root children are never found, and a 'search until found' loop runs forever.
lessons.fix: Get shared nodes through a group (get_tree().get_first_node_in_group()), a known path from get_tree().root, or by letting the owner register them. If you must search the whole tree, start at get_tree().root, keep the result, and repeat a failed search only every 20 s or so.
lessons.test: Add a DirectionalLight3D as a child of the root next to the current scene and check that the lookup finds it on the first call.

lessons.title: Merge identical procedural parts once and share the ArrayMesh
lessons.symptom: About 130 uniformed characters appearing near a training area froze the game for 2 seconds.
lessons.cause: Each character merged its 40 or so parts into its own ArrayMesh with SurfaceTool.append_from() and commit(). Every new mesh is built in GDScript and uploaded to the GPU on its own, although most characters were identical.
lessons.fix: Build a key from the parts (mesh class, name, transform, colour) and keep the committed ArrayMesh, its part list and its materials in a static cache; identical characters reuse the same resources. Put a limit on the cache size.
lessons.test: Spawn the same group twice; the second spawn should be much faster and its MeshInstance3D nodes should share mesh resources.

lessons.title: Fill heightmap collision with packed-array slices, not a loop over every cell
lessons.symptom: When the player flew into a mountain area, single frames took up to 95 ms; each 129 by 129 collision tile took 8 to 10 ms to fill, and several new tiles arrived at once.
lessons.cause: The HeightMapShape3D data was filled one float at a time in GDScript, adding a constant base height to every cell. Per-element loops in GDScript are slow at this size, and all tiles in range were built in the same frame.
lessons.fix: Copy each row with PackedFloat32Array.slice() and append_array(), pad the edge by repeating the last value, and move constant offsets into the body's position instead of the data. Compute the heights on a worker thread and add at most one new collision body per frame.
lessons.test: Time one tile before and after, and compare raycast hits at a few points; the world heights must be identical.

lessons.title: Test a HUD overlay together with the other overlays in the same screen corner
lessons.symptom: A picture-in-picture frame never showed up in the game, although its own test passed every check.
lessons.cause: A round minimap in the same corner lived on a CanvasLayer with a higher layer index and covered the frame completely. The isolated test had no minimap, so it could not see the problem.
lessons.fix: Give overlays a documented layer order, place them relative to each other by reading the other control's get_global_rect(), redo the layout when that control appears or changes size, and test with the full HUD present. A small log of the frame's global rect and visibility found the cause after one run.
lessons.test: Add the other overlay to the test and check that the rectangles do not intersect and that the new layer is higher.

lessons.title: Draw a head-up display in the combiner glass's own UV space, not full screen
lessons.symptom: The head-up display sat off centre on its glass at some resolutions and scales, and its horizon line did not lie on the real horizon.
lessons.cause: The symbols were drawn into a SubViewport the size of the screen and sampled with screen-space coordinates in the glass shader, so the result depended on window size, content scale and camera. The pilot's eye was also 9 cm above the glass centre, so the line of sight passed over the glass.
lessons.fix: Use a fixed-size SubViewport texture that maps onto the glass's own texture coordinates and sample it with UV. Place each symbol by intersecting the ray from the eye to the target with the glass plane, and get pixels per radian from the eye's distance to that plane. Put the camera at the sight's design eye. The fixed texture is also much cheaper than a screen-sized one.
lessons.test: Render the cockpit at several window sizes and scales and check that the horizon symbol lies on the real horizon and the symbols stay centred on the glass.

lessons.title: An additive gunsight fades away against a bright sky; mix it with alpha instead
lessons.symptom: The reflector sight was hard to see whenever the aircraft pointed at a bright sky or clouds.
lessons.cause: The sight was drawn with additive blending, which can only brighten the background; on a nearly white sky there is nothing left to add.
lessons.fix: Draw the symbols with mix blending and an alpha (render_mode blend_mix), with a soft glow ring around the lines and a very light tint on the glass, so they stay readable on any background.
lessons.test: Render the sight against a white sky, a dark sky and terrain and check the contrast of the symbol in each.

lessons.title: Hide parts that one camera must never see with render layers and its cull mask
lessons.symptom: Engine parts inside the fuselage showed through the cockpit floor from the pilot's view, and a sensor camera under a large aircraft looked straight into the aircraft's own skin.
lessons.cause: The internal parts and the vehicle's own hull were on the same render layer as the rest of the world, so every camera drew them.
lessons.fix: Put such meshes on their own bit of VisualInstance3D.layers and clear that bit from the cull_mask of the pilot or sensor camera; other cameras still render them.
lessons.test: Render from the pilot eye and the sensor camera and check the parts are absent, then from the outside camera and check they are present.

lessons.title: A CylinderMesh turned +90 degrees about X has its top at +Z, the back of a -Z-forward model
lessons.symptom: The vapour cone around a jet's canopy was wide at the front and narrow towards the tail, the wrong way round.
lessons.cause: CylinderMesh puts top_radius at +Y. Rotating the mesh +90 degrees about X sends +Y to +Z, and in a model that faces -Z, +Z points backwards, so top_radius ended up at the tail.
lessons.fix: Work out where each end goes after the rotation and set top_radius and bottom_radius for that; write the axis convention next to the code.
lessons.test: After rotating, transform a point of the top ring and check it lies behind (larger Z than) the bottom ring.

lessons.title: Check from the eye that every gauge face sits in front of the panel plate
lessons.symptom: The cockpit gauges 'did not work': only the sunken back of each instrument showed, and a cover strip hid two more dials. In another cockpit the faces sat 4 mm behind the panel.
lessons.cause: The generator placed the dial faces 10 mm deep inside a 12 mm panel plate, and a black close-out strip stood 1.5 cm in front of the panel's top edge. Renders from a distance did not show it.
lessons.fix: Put dial faces 1 mm in front of the plate and close-out strips behind the panel plane. Add a check that takes a few points per needle (centre and near the rim) and fails when any cockpit triangle lies between the needle and 2 cm in front of it.
lessons.test: The check failed five dials on the broken build and passed all variants after the fix.

lessons.title: Test a hull's winding against the outward direction, not against another surface
lessons.symptom: The upper hull of a large yacht could be seen through from outside. After that fix, the underwater hull turned out to be inside out too and needed a second release.
lessons.cause: Godot draws triangles whose vertices run clockwise as seen from the front and culls the others. The generator emitted some surfaces the other way round, and the first repair compared them with the antifouling surface as the 'known good' reference, which was itself reversed.
lessons.fix: For every surface, compute each triangle's geometric normal and compare it with the direction from the hull's centre line to the triangle; flip the surfaces where most triangles face inward, in every level of detail. Keep the check as a test.
lessons.test: Per material, count the share of triangles that face outward and require at least 75 % for every exterior surface.

lessons.title: Let the model builder measure what it built, per part, against the spec
lessons.symptom: A large aircraft came out 40 % too long, with a beam floating 20 m in front of its nose; on a warship a small radar dome had 46,000 triangles.
lessons.cause: One nose part added its offset twice, and round parts were refined twice by nested detail settings. Nothing compared the result with the target sizes or the triangle budget.
lessons.fix: After every build, write the overall bounds and the size and triangle count of each part next to the spec values, and fail the build when a size is more than a few percent off or a part goes over its budget.
lessons.test: Feed the builder a part with a doubled offset and check that the build fails.

lessons.title: A control surface on a swept wing must turn about its own hinge line
lessons.symptom: The spoilers, flaps and rudders swung loose above the wing, all turning about the same straight sideways axis.
lessons.cause: The rig file that listed the hinges had not been regenerated, and the runtime silently fell back to turning each part about the body's X axis. On a swept wing the hinge line is not parallel to that axis.
lessons.fix: Give each moving surface a pivot Node3D whose origin is on the hinge and whose local X axis lies along the hinge line, with the mesh as its child, and turn it with rotate_object_local(Vector3.RIGHT, angle). Treat a missing hinge as an error instead of a fallback and check the hinge count of every variant.
lessons.test: Turn every surface by a test angle and check that its vertices on the hinge line do not move.

lessons.title: Ground collision that is streamed in must follow every moving body, not only the player
lessons.symptom: Cars and other vehicles fell through the ground anywhere outside a small area, and bridges had no collision at all.
lessons.cause: Collision tiles were only built within 256 m of the walking player, so any RigidBody3D, VehicleBody3D or CharacterBody3D elsewhere had nothing under it.
lessons.fix: Keep collision tiles around every active body, with a radius of about 70 m plus the distance it will travel in the next 2.5 s. Build them from the same heights and road profiles as the visible ground, and add deck shapes for bridges and ramps.
lessons.test: Drop crates on roads and bridges far from the player and check they stay on the surface.

lessons.title: A road ribbon over a coarse heightmap needs the terrain shaped to the road
lessons.symptom: The roads floated above the verge or were buried, with steps and holes along the edges; 1.2 % of the measured points floated more than 25 cm.
lessons.cause: The road was a flat ribbon 6 cm above the terrain at its points, which were about 15 m apart, but between them and at the edges the ground followed a 32 m grid that cannot follow a road, least of all where two roads run close together (a dike road and one at its foot).
lessons.fix: Flatten the terrain under every road to the road profile with a 1:1.5 embankment limited to a few metres, lift road points where the terrain still pokes through, add a sloped verge mesh along the ribbon, and use the exact road profile in the collision.
lessons.test: Raycast a few hundred random road points, centre and edges: after the fix the 95th percentile was 2.9 cm, with no misses.

lessons.title: Give inland water its own surface instead of relying on the sea plane
lessons.symptom: The rivers and lakes had no visible water, or water that dropped 0.8 m with the tide, carried ocean waves and turned almost transparent in shallow places.
lessons.cause: The inland water relied on the global sea layer, which moves with the tide and is shaded for open sea; inland, the sea also drew over land.
lessons.fix: Build inland water as its own meshes at its own level (rivers with flowing texture coordinates), deepen the bed where needed, and mask the sea shader out of land and inland water with a coarse mask texture.
lessons.test: Render at high and low tide and check that the inland level stays put and the sea no longer draws over land.

lessons.title: Gameplay queries must read the same data that builds what is drawn
lessons.symptom: A boat started on a railway station because the water test said there was water there.
lessons.cause: The 'is water' query read an older water grid that no longer matched the visible water, so spawn points that were on land passed the test.
lessons.fix: Answer water and ground queries from the same mask or height function that builds the visible mesh and the collision; check the visible data first and fall back to old data only where there is none. Move spawn points onto the current data.
lessons.test: Query many points and compare with the mesh: in one area 30 of 30 downward raycasts hit the visible terrain within 0.18 m.

lessons.title: Turning a builder into a coroutine changes every caller that reads its result
lessons.symptom: After a station hall was built over several frames to avoid a stutter, a test counted 0 meshes in the hall, and a prebuilt scene could be handed over half built.
lessons.cause: A function that contains await returns to its caller at the first await. Code that called it without await read the node right after the call, before the rest of the build had run.
lessons.fix: Await the builder, or let it set a done flag or emit a signal at the end and make callers wait for that. When a half-built prebuild is needed early, throw it away and build fresh instead of using it, and check is_inside_tree() after every await.
lessons.test: Check the result both right after the call and after awaiting it; tests must wait for the done flag (or enough frames) before counting.
errors: is a coroutine, so it must be called with "await"

lessons.title: A node you parent under someone else's camera is freed with that camera
lessons.symptom: A full-screen snow veil stopped working, with errors, after the player boarded a helicopter from the walking view.
