lessons.cause: The effect parented its veil quad under the active Camera3D. The walking camera was freed when the player boarded, the veil was freed with it, and the effect still used its reference.
lessons.fix: Check is_instance_valid() before every use and rebuild the node (keep the material), or keep the node under your own parent and copy the active camera's transform each frame.
lessons.test: Free the active camera while the effect is on and check that the effect keeps drawing without errors.

lessons.title: A scene fingerprint shows that a loading refactor kept the same world
lessons.symptom: Work that moved world building onto threads and across frames could change the world without anyone noticing, and there was no way to show that it had not.
lessons.cause: Node names, order and timing differ between runs: nodes added without a name get generated names with a counter, and traffic, ships and rotors move all the time.
lessons.fix: Write one row per node: its path with the generated counters removed, class, script, visibility, global position rounded to 1 cm, basis to 0.001, the mesh resource or its surface count and AABB, and hashes of MultiMesh transforms and collision shape data. Take two snapshots 20 s apart; rows that change are dynamic and only counted. Hash the static rows per top-level module and compare runs. Walk the tree in slices of a few milliseconds and do the sorting and hashing on a worker thread.
lessons.test: Reload the same world with 50 extra unnamed nodes and get the same hash; move one node 1 cm and see only its module change.

lessons.title: When you change only visuals, hash the collision geometry before and after
lessons.symptom: A large visual upgrade of eleven stations had to leave the walkable floors and platform edges exactly as they were.
lessons.cause: Visual and collision geometry were built by the same code paths, so a visual change could move a floor or open a gap without showing in renders.
lessons.fix: Hash all collision triangles (and other gameplay surfaces) per station with the upgrade on and with it switched off, and require equal hashes; list any new collision on purpose (here only new doors and columns).
lessons.test: The hash comparison runs in the same headless test as the build, for every station.

lessons.title: A *.res rule in .gitignore keeps Godot's binary resources out of the repository
lessons.symptom: A fresh checkout of a ship had no materials or textures, although everything worked on the machine that built it.
lessons.cause: The repository ignored *.res, which is also the extension of Godot's binary resources (materials, textures and meshes saved with ResourceSaver), so they were never committed.
lessons.fix: Do not ignore *.res; ignore the .godot/ cache folder and build output instead. If a file must be added despite an ignore rule, add it explicitly, and test with a clean clone.
lessons.test: Make a fresh clone in an empty folder, import it, load the scene headless and check for missing dependency errors.

lessons.title: Run headless tests on a shipped pack with the matching Godot binary or a small test pack
lessons.symptom: Passing a test script to the shipped game executable with --headless -s simply started the game, and on Windows the output of the normal executable could not be captured from a pipe.
lessons.cause: The exported executable runs its own project: it ignored the script argument and loaded its main scene. The Windows GUI build does not write to a console pipe the way the console build does.
lessons.fix: Use the official Godot binary of exactly the same version (the console variant on Windows) with --main-pack pointing at the shipped pack and -s for the test. Or build a small test pack with its own project settings and main scene that calls ProjectSettings.load_resource_pack() for the shipped pack and the overlay under test. Wait one frame before adding nodes to the root. Link a very large pack instead of copying it.
lessons.test: The test prints an explicit pass line, and the runner fails when the line is missing.

lessons.title: Validate a baked cache before you build the geometry it will replace
lessons.symptom: Entering a train cab took 1.7 s although the finished cab came from baked meshes; cabs whose bake no longer matched silently took 2 to 15 s in one frame.
lessons.cause: The full procedural cab (walls, normals, window frames) was generated first and then completely replaced by the baked meshes. When a lever had moved since the bake, validation failed and the code quietly built everything at full detail.
lessons.fix: Check the bake first. If it is valid, build only what applying it needs (node names, surface counts, materials, frames of moving parts), using one-triangle stub surfaces, and then apply the bake. When it does not match, log a warning with the reason and rebake.
lessons.test: Hash names, transforms and mesh data after the light build and after the full build (they must be equal), and test the fallback with a deliberately broken manifest.

lessons.title: When the camera can fly, stream content by the 3D distance its shaders cull by
lessons.symptom: A large aircraft flying at 2,500 m ran at about 20 fps: trees near the ground were built and removed every frame, and underground station halls under the aircraft were built in frames of 330 ms.
lessons.cause: The streaming rings used horizontal distance from the camera, while the tree shaders culled by 3D distance, so the near rings were built but never seen. The underground parts were built because they were horizontally close.
lessons.fix: Include the camera's height above the highest ground around it in the streaming distance, skip content that cannot be seen from above (underground halls when the camera is more than about 500 m above the ground), and cap the number of new nodes per frame.
lessons.test: Fly at several altitudes and log the per-frame build time and node counts of each streaming system.

lessons.title: Drive child parts with local transforms from cached rest values, not by writing global_transform
lessons.symptom: Far from the origin (about 70 km out) the bogies of a train slowly drifted away from the car body.
lessons.cause: Code set each bogie's global_transform every frame. At that distance the round trip through 32-bit world coordinates loses millimetres, and the error was written back into the local position, where it piled up.
lessons.fix: Store each part's rest position and basis once, keep its position at the rest value, and set only the local rotation (inverse parent basis times target basis).
lessons.test: Run the train for a long time far from the origin and check that the local positions stay exactly at their rest values.

lessons.title: A speed-limit look-ahead must reach further than the braking distance from top speed
lessons.symptom: A very fast train got an emergency brake intervention before a curve, dropping from about 600 to 290 km/h.
lessons.cause: The protection system looked 2.5 km ahead, but at that speed the train needed about 3.5 km to slow down for the curve, so the limit appeared too late to brake normally.
lessons.fix: Lower the allowed speed gradually before each restriction at the planned deceleration (a braking curve of 1.4 m/s┬▓ here), or make the look-ahead at least the braking distance from maximum speed.
lessons.test: Drive at full speed into every curve on every line and count interventions (expect zero).

lessons.title: Re-check gradients after pinning fixed heights such as station floors into a profile
lessons.symptom: A generated rail line had a 20 % kink at the end of a platform.
lessons.cause: The vertical profile was first smoothed to the gradient limit, and only then was a fixed station floor imposed, higher than the slope next to it allowed.
lessons.fix: After setting fixed points, run a pass that enforces the maximum gradient outward from them (here only by lowering, so tunnel cover stays enough), then check gradient and cover along the whole line.
lessons.test: Check the gradient between every pair of profile points and the cover above every tunnel point.

lessons.title: Base an 'on the deck' test on where the body really rests, not on the model's nominal height
lessons.symptom: A helicopter parked on a moving yacht slid away when the player got in, and the key to get out did nothing.
lessons.cause: The 'on deck' test allowed only 0.35 m around the model's nominal height, but the skid collider made the helicopter rest higher, so it did not count as on deck and was not held. A take-off flag left over from boarding also counted as lifting.
lessons.fix: Measure the rest height of the real collision shapes on the deck and use an asymmetric band around it (here -0.6 to +1.2 m). Count only real pilot input (collective up with the rotor at speed) as lifting, and give a held body the deck's velocity at that point, not zero.
lessons.test: In a test, get in, wait and get out on a deck moving at 8 knots, also in a turn, and check that nothing slides and exiting works.

lessons.title: Repeat a prebuilt track or tube segment with MultiMesh and pass the distance in custom data
lessons.symptom: Building each 240 m piece of tube took 2.2 ms every 0.7 s at full speed, and the faceted walls showed a fan of dark stripes.
lessons.cause: Every piece was generated vertex by vertex in GDScript, with flat faces whose colour changed every few faces.
lessons.fix: Build one 10 m segment template once and place it as MultiMesh instances along the path. Put the distance along the path in instance custom data, wrapped with fposmod() to keep float precision, so a shader can continue seams and panel lines across instances. Set MultiMesh.use_custom_data before instance_count.
lessons.test: Time a piece build (2.2 ms to 0.3 ms here) and check that segment ends follow the path within a few millimetres.

lessons.title: Check the byte size of an asynchronous texture readback; RGB8 textures come back as RGBA8
lessons.symptom: Reading textures back for a compression cache stalled frames by 2 to 15 ms each, 278 times in the first minute.
lessons.cause: ImageTexture.get_image() waits for the GPU. The asynchronous path (RenderingServer.texture_get_rd_texture() with RenderingDevice.texture_get_data_async()) avoids the wait, but textures uploaded as RGB8 are stored as RGBA8 on the GPU, so their bytes do not match the Image layout.
lessons.fix: Use the asynchronous readback, move the callback to the main thread with call_deferred(), compute the expected size from width, height, format and mipmaps, and build the Image with Image.create_from_data() only when the size matches. Read RGB8 and any mismatch the old way, or keep their source images.
lessons.test: Hash images read both ways for RGBA8, RGB8 and single-channel textures with and without mipmaps; they must equal the source images.

lessons.title: Work written inside assert() does not run in a release export
lessons.symptom: Trees showed as white, opaque cards in the exported release game, while every editor and debug run looked right. Both leaf atlases came out empty.
lessons.cause: The PNG decode (Image.load_png_from_buffer()) was written inside the assert() condition. Godot only evaluates assert() in debug builds, so in the release export the decode never ran, the Image stayed empty and the shader sampled nothing.
lessons.fix: Do the work first and keep its result in a variable; then check that value with if and push_error(). An assert() may only read values that already exist. Accept rendering and loading fixes on the release export template, because an editor or debug binary hides this.
lessons.test: Run the exported release build on the scene and check that the textures are bound and not empty. Search the code for assert( conditions that call a method that loads, decodes, adds or sets something.

lessons.title: Values from weakref(), call() and Callable.call() are Variant, so an inferred type fails
lessons.symptom: Scripts that had worked before failed to compile under Godot 4.7: a QA script that kept a weakref() and a cab script that kept the result of a Callable.call() could not be loaded.
lessons.cause: weakref(), Object.call(), Object.get() and Callable.call() return Variant. A variable declared with an inferred type then gets its type from a Variant, and in Godot 4.7 the setting debug/gdscript/warnings/inference_on_variant defaults to Error, so the script does not compile.
lessons.fix: Write the type you expect: WeakRef for weakref(), the node or value type for call() results, or cast with as. Do not lower the warning level to make the error go away.
lessons.test: Compile every script headless; the warning must not appear.
errors: The variable type is being inferred from a Variant value

lessons.title: Reach a parent feature that only some base versions have through has_method() and call()
lessons.symptom: Two add-ons had to run on an older and a newer version of the same base script. A direct call to a helper that only the newer base has did not compile on the old base, and passing the newer base's extra argument to super did not compile there either; a test that loaded it hung.
lessons.cause: GDScript resolves calls on self and super when it compiles: an unknown function is a parse error, too many arguments for super is a parse error, and super cannot be called dynamically (a Callable to a super method is also a parse error).
lessons.fix: Give the override the new parameter with the same name and default, pass super only the arguments the oldest base accepts, and reach optional base features with has_method() plus call() so the script compiles on both. Keep a compile matrix: base alone, base plus each add-on, and all together, on both base versions.
lessons.test: Compile each combination headless and require zero new errors compared with the bare base.
errors: The function signature doesn't match the parent

lessons.title: To add a button to a menu you do not own, watch node_added and insert deferred on every rebuild
lessons.symptom: An add-on button inserted once into the main menu disappeared as soon as the menu rebuilt its page, and a first version never found its anchor button by name.
lessons.cause: The menu cleared and rebuilt its pages, which freed the injected button. SceneTree.node_added fires inside add_child(), before the menu code that called add_child() has set the button's name and text, so a check made right away sees a default name.
lessons.fix: Use an autoload that connects to SceneTree.node_added, checks candidate nodes with call_deferred(), skips nodes that are queued for deletion, and inserts next to the anchor only when the page does not already hold its button. It then works again on every rebuild without editing the menu script.
lessons.test: Rebuild the page several times and check that the button exists exactly once, against a stand-in of the menu and against the real one.

lessons.title: Rotation about +Y is counterclockwise; a compass heading is its negative
lessons.symptom: New cockpit compass displays turned the wrong way when they were fed the aircraft's heading value, which turned out to be the raw yaw; older displays still showed that raw value.
lessons.cause: In Godot a positive rotation about +Y turns a node counterclockwise seen from above, while a compass heading grows clockwise. With -Z as north, a node rotated +90 degrees faces west. Displays that showed the raw yaw were mirrored.
lessons.fix: Convert once, in one helper: heading in degrees is the negative yaw, wrapped to 0..360 with fposmod(); give the helper a test and use it for every display, map and autopilot.
lessons.test: Point the body at -Z, +X, +Z and -X and expect 0, 90, 180 and 270.

lessons.title: Render layer bits are shared by every system: keep a table and re-apply layers after reparenting
lessons.symptom: A pilot figure was hidden from the cockpit camera by moving it to a spare render layer, but a sensor camera that also skipped that layer could then not see a parked aircraft whose exterior used the same bit. Elsewhere an exterior branch moved under the cockpit lost its own layer and its shadows.
lessons.cause: VisualInstance3D.layers, Camera3D.cull_mask and the masks of lights and decals all read the same 20 bits, and one system's meaning of a bit is invisible to another. Code that walks a subtree, such as setting cockpit layers or turning cast_shadow off for interior parts, also hits a branch that is later moved into that subtree.
lessons.fix: Keep one table of what each bit means and check every new use against it. After reparenting a branch, apply its own layers again and leave it out of interior-only optimisations.
lessons.test: List layers and cast_shadow per node group before and after the change and compare.

lessons.title: A billboard that grows with distance needs billboard_keep_scale
lessons.symptom: Navigation and obstacle lights were invisible at night from a few kilometres, although each lamp had a glow sprite that was scaled up with distance.
lessons.cause: When billboard_mode is enabled, BaseMaterial3D drops the mesh's scale unless billboard_keep_scale is on, so the sprite kept its unscaled size and became smaller than a pixel far away. A real lamp of 0.4 m is already below a pixel at that range.
lessons.fix: Turn on billboard_keep_scale, scale the sprite with distance to a fixed angular size (about 0.2 degrees, with a minimum size), use an unshaded additive material, and keep real OmniLight3D nodes only for lights near the camera.
lessons.test: Render the lights at night from 1, 3 and 6 km and count lit pixels per lamp.

lessons.title: Smooth metallic materials without surface detail take the colour of the sky
lessons.symptom: In a cockpit, metal parts looked blue, although their albedo was neutral grey.
lessons.cause: The material was mostly metallic, with roughness about 0.29 and an effectively flat surface, so it acted as a mirror and showed the blue sky. Its albedo and roughness maps each held one single colour.
lessons.fix: Painted or coated metal is not metallic: use metallic 0 and the paint's roughness. Keep metallic for bare metal only, add roughness variation that follows the normal map, and check colours under a neutral grey environment as well as the game sky.
lessons.test: Render the part under a grey sky and under the game sky and compare its colour.

lessons.title: A pooled GPUParticles3D fed with emit_particle() needs two frames of warm-up and a world-sized visibility box
lessons.symptom: The first effects after a scene start did not appear, and effects far from the emitter node vanished when that node left the screen.
lessons.cause: emit_particle() calls in the first frame after the GPUParticles3D was created were lost; it worked, with emitting off, from the second frame on. A pooled emitter with local_coords off draws its particles anywhere in the world, but culling, collision and attraction use its visibility_aabb, which defaults to 8 m around the node.
lessons.fix: Count frames after creating the pool and drop or queue emits until two frames have passed. Set visibility_aabb to cover the whole play area for world-space pools, keep emitting off, and use emit_particle() for every burst.
lessons.test: Emit at frames 0, 1 and 2 after creation and count live particles; emit 5 km away with the pool node behind the camera.

lessons.title: Particle attractors push every particle system unless you give your particles a layer bit
lessons.symptom: A new rotor-downwash flow field for smoke would also have pushed the existing rotor-wash spray, and scorch decals projected onto the smoke itself.
lessons.cause: The cull_mask of particle attractor nodes and Decal.cull_mask default to all layers, so an attractor acts on every GPUParticles3D whose layers match and a decal projects onto every visual.
lessons.fix: Put your effect particles on layer 1 plus one dedicated bit, set the attractors' cull_mask to that bit only, and remove the bit from the decals' cull_mask. For a vector-field attractor, Godot reads the texture as rgb times 2 minus 1, a positive strength pushes along the vector, and image row 0 is the bottom of the box.
lessons.test: Hover over the new smoke and over the old spray with the field on and off and compare particle positions.

lessons.title: Check albedo values in the engine: a near-black surface reads as a hole
lessons.symptom: The roofs of small beach huts looked upside down in the game, like an inverted V, although geometry and normals were correct.
lessons.cause: The roof texture had an albedo of about 0.02. Under the game's lighting it showed as a dark gap; the offline renderer used for previews made it look lighter, so it passed review there.
lessons.fix: Keep albedo within a physical range (roughly 0.04 to 0.9), give dark materials texture and lighter edge trims, and review assets in Godot with the game's lighting, not only in the modelling tool.
lessons.test: Report the mean albedo per material and flag values below about 0.04.

lessons.title: A resource pack mounted at runtime must register its uid values
lessons.symptom: Scenes from an add-on pack, and models appended to a shipped pack later, printed one warning per texture or script reference: invalid UID, using text path instead.
lessons.cause: Resources reference each other by uid, and the game's UID cache is written at export time. Resources added later with ProjectSettings.load_resource_pack() or appended to the pack are not in it, so Godot falls back to the text path and warns.
lessons.fix: When building the add-on pack, read the uid from each resource's import file and store a uid-to-path map. On mount, call ResourceUID.add_id() for every id that ResourceUID.has_id() does not know, never overriding an existing one. Load the pack with file replacement off (second argument false), leave out the project settings, the UID cache and the global class cache, and load the loader as an autoload from an override file next to the executable, so the shipped pack stays untouched.
lessons.test: Start the exported game with the add-on and count UID warnings (zero) and shadowed game files (zero).

lessons.title: Vertex colours in a glTF act as an albedo multiplier; set the flag per surface yourself
lessons.symptom: Ambient occlusion baked into the vertex colours also darkened glass, lamps and rubber. On another model, wetness and algae stored in vertex colours did not show on some surfaces.
lessons.cause: Godot's glTF importer turns on vertex_color_use_as_albedo for materials of primitives that carry vertex colours, so whatever is in that channel multiplies the albedo; it did not do this reliably for every material (one model's first material stayed off). A surface without vertex colours reads COLOR as white.
lessons.fix: Store only data that is safe as a multiplier in the RGB of the vertex colours (grey AO), keep other data in alpha or in UV channels for your own shaders, and after loading set vertex_color_use_as_albedo per surface from ArrayMesh.surface_get_format() and Mesh.ARRAY_FORMAT_COLOR. Bake AO for all levels of detail on one shared grid so it does not jump at the switch.
lessons.test: After import, list every surface with its colour format bit and its material flag.

lessons.title: SurfaceTool.append_from() carries vertex channels that only some merged parts have
lessons.symptom: A batched control stick showed two visible vertex-channel errors in the render, although every assert in the test passed.
lessons.cause: The source meshes were mixed: some were generated with skin channels (bones and weights) and some without. append_from() merges each source's vertex format into the builder, so the rigid batch got empty bone and weight channels and mismatched attributes.
lessons.fix: For a rigid batch, copy only the attributes you render: per index call set_normal() (transformed by the inverse transpose of the part's basis), set_tangent(), set_uv() and set_color() before add_vertex(), then index() and commit(). Or strip skin channels from the sources first.
lessons.test: Render the batch next to the unbatched parts and diff the images; check that the committed surface format has no bone or weight bits.

lessons.title: Normal-mapped meshes need UV coordinates and tangents in the exported file
lessons.symptom: A model export was rejected because the exporter could not calculate tangents, a trim part had no UV layer, and a procedural character body lit its normal-mapped fabric wrongly.
lessons.cause: Tangents are computed per triangle from UV coordinates and normals. Faces with more than four corners, a missing UV layer or a procedural ArrayMesh without a tangent array leave none, so Godot has no tangent basis for the normal map.
lessons.fix: Triangulate the export copy and give every normal-mapped part a UV layer before exporting. For procedural meshes in Godot, set normals and UV coordinates and then call SurfaceTool.generate_tangents().
lessons.test: A validator that fails when a surface with a normal-mapped material has no tangent array.

lessons.title: Check every boolean cut and retry, because it can fail without an error
lessons.symptom: A helicopter hull lost most of its faces after an exact boolean cut for a window, and the build reported nothing.
lessons.cause: Exact booleans can collapse on coplanar or touching faces and still return a mesh.
lessons.fix: After each cut, compare volume, face count and bounds with the input. On failure retry with a sub-millimetre offset on the cutter or with another cut order, and stop the build if no variant passes.
lessons.test: Unit test the cutter with a coplanar case and expect the retry path to produce a valid result.

lessons.title: Re-run clearance checks on every decimated level of detail
lessons.symptom: The lower levels of detail of a glareshield shroud cut into instruments again: five intersections in LOD1 and eight in LOD2, while LOD0 was clean.
lessons.cause: The decimator moved the vertices of the carefully cut clearance edges.
lessons.fix: Check intersections per level against everything around the part in world space. For small parts, keep the validated mesh in LOD1 and leave the part out of LOD2 instead of decimating it, and record that choice so a later export cannot bring the rejected mesh back.
lessons.test: A BVH overlap test of each level of detail against all neighbouring meshes.

lessons.title: Move every moving part through its whole range and check it against the real skin and its neighbours
lessons.symptom: A sliding door left its handle floating in the opening, retracted tyres poked 4 to 11 cm through closed gear doors, and a fire-control director would have hit the mast legs.
lessons.cause: Parts were checked in their rest pose only. The handle was part of the static rail mesh instead of a child of the door node; the gear solver kept the tyres above a flat bay box instead of the real lower hull surface.
lessons.fix: Put everything that moves with a part under that part's node. In the builder, sweep each moving part through its full range against the real surfaces and neighbouring parts, and set its limits from the sweep (here the director was limited to 30 degrees either side).
lessons.test: Automated sweep with the maximum protrusion and minimum clearance per part (the gear reached 1.1 cm), plus renders at the end positions.

lessons.title: A compensation for a non-uniform parent scale shears rotated children
lessons.symptom: In a cockpit, cable looms and grab handles stood 15 to 21 degrees out of square.
lessons.cause: The cockpit root had a non-uniform scale (about 0.54, 0.8, 0.8), and each child's rotation was multiplied by the inverse of that scale. A rotation combined with a non-uniform scale is no longer a rotation, so the local bases became sheared, with column lengths between 1.25 and 1.64.
lessons.fix: Avoid non-uniform scale on nodes that have rotated children; bake the scale into the meshes. If a compensation is needed, split it into an orthonormal rotation (Basis.orthonormalized()) and a separate scale.
lessons.test: For every node, the dot products of its normalised basis columns must be close to zero.

lessons.title: Sample outlines and unwrap lofted bodies by arc length, not by parameter
lessons.symptom: Rubber window seals and glass edges wavered along long straight sides, and flat fuselage sides got stretched texels.
lessons.cause: Points were spaced evenly in the curve parameter or in angle, which bunches them in tight bends and spreads them on straight runs.
lessons.fix: Sample every outline again at equal arc length (every 12 mm here) before building seals and cuts, and let the V coordinate of a lofted body follow the cumulative circumference so flat walls and bends get the same texel density; put the seam where it is not seen.
lessons.test: Measure the largest distance between the seal and the true outline, and the texel density per face.

lessons.title: Find inside-out faces by rendering back faces in a loud colour from many sides
lessons.symptom: Players could see through a ship's hull and deck, and the fault had been there since the first version.
lessons.cause: The generator's normals and triangle winding pointed inward on several parts (hull, deck, rims, dishes), so Godot culled the faces that should be seen.
lessons.fix: Fix the winding where the surface is built (the cross product times the side sign) and add a check: render the model from 16 directions with back faces drawn bright magenta (cull disabled, the front-facing shader built-in decides the colour) and fail above a small share of magenta pixels (0.05 % was used).
lessons.test: Magenta pixel share per view, tracked between versions.

lessons.title: A display surface needs its own planar, upright UV map
lessons.symptom: In a cockpit, the displays showed their image upside down and only partly.
lessons.cause: The screen faces were rounded boxes with the modelling tool's default cube unwrap, so the viewport texture landed rotated and cut off on the visible face.
lessons.fix: Give display faces their own planar UV coordinates from 0 to 1, upright as seen from the pilot's eye. If the model cannot be rebuilt, project the UV coordinates at bind time (planar toward the eye) for surfaces marked as screens.
lessons.test: Show a test pattern with labelled corners on every screen and render it from the seat.

lessons.title: Far tiles must get the same filters and shader inputs as near chunks
lessons.symptom: Distant trees stood still while near trees swayed, and the switch at chunk borders popped. Elsewhere forest and dunes appeared in the distance and vanished when the area loaded.
lessons.cause: The far foliage tiles used their own ShaderMaterial, and only the near materials received the wind and time parameters each frame. The far tile builder also skipped the coast filter that the near chunks applied.
lessons.fix: Build near and far from one rule set, and feed time and wind as global shader uniforms (RenderingServer.global_shader_parameter_set()) so every material at every level of detail gets them; otherwise set them on every material in the chain.
lessons.test: Fly across a chunk border in wind and compare the last near frame with the first far frame; list which materials received each parameter.

lessons.title: Check a placed object against moving routes for every scenario seed, not just one
lessons.symptom: A wind farm placed well clear of the fleet had a frigate sailing straight through a turbine with the default seed, and moving the farm 500 m landward still left only 5 m with another seed.
lessons.cause: The ship routes and formation offsets came from the scenario seed, so the clearance depended on the seed, and it had been checked by eye with one seed.
lessons.fix: Run the real route and formation code headless for many seeds (301 scenarios with 1500 points each here) and require a margin of half the hull length plus the rotor radius in the worst case; choose the site from that table.
lessons.test: Store the smallest clearance per seed and fail when any seed is under the margin.

lessons.title: Code that remembers the last time must handle a clock that jumps back
lessons.symptom: A ship's wake disappeared for good after a new mission or a reload.
lessons.cause: The wake added a point only when at least one sample interval had passed since the stored last time. A new mission or a load set the clock back to a smaller value, the stored time was never reset, so the difference stayed negative and no point was ever added again.
lessons.fix: When the current time is lower than the stored one, treat it as a new session: clear the trail and reset the stored time. Prefer a monotonic source such as accumulated delta for effects.
lessons.test: Run a mission, start a new one and check that the effect is back.

lessons.title: Translate enum values between systems explicitly; a clamp maps unknown values to the extreme
lessons.symptom: Rain, fog, sleet and evening light gave a storm sea with waves up to 8.9 m, and the ships pitched accordingly.
lessons.cause: The weather system numbered its states 0 to 7, the sea system only knew 0 to 3 and clamped higher numbers, so every state above 3 became the last one, storm.
lessons.fix: Map one system's states to the other with an explicit table at the boundary (or pass names), and fail loudly on an unknown value instead of clamping.
lessons.test: Feed every weather state through the bridge and check the resulting sea state and wave height.

lessons.title: Do not gate a control assist on a smoothed input; it engages too late
lessons.symptom: A stability assist meant to hold the attitude after the stick was released barely did anything.
lessons.cause: It waited until the smoothed stick value fell below 0.03, and the smoothing decays slowly, so the assist hardly ever got the chance to act.
lessons.fix: Engage on the release itself (raw input inside the dead zone, or the core's idle-time counter above zero) and let the smoothed value only shape the output.
lessons.test: Use scripted input: release the stick and measure the time until the assist engages and how much the rate decays.

lessons.title: Apply mouse look once per rendered frame so it does not depend on the frame rate
lessons.symptom: A targeting camera and sensor display jittered, and the same mouse movement gave different results at different frame rates.
lessons.cause: Mouse input was filtered where physics steps run, so a rendered frame applied it zero, one or several times, and render cameras were also fed back through their parent.
lessons.fix: Add up the relative mouse motion as it arrives, filter and apply it once per rendered frame, hold it stable between physics steps, and let render cameras follow the interpolated vehicle pose in _process.
lessons.test: Replay the same mouse command at 30, 60 and 120 fps and compare the end orientation; measure drift of the camera against the cockpit over 90 frames.

lessons.title: An unreachable path goal can start a full A* search every frame
lessons.symptom: One onlooker at an accident scene made frames take 152 ms.
lessons.cause: Its goal cell lay on a car roof that the ground grid cannot reach, so A* searched about 6000 nodes, failed, and tried again the next frame.
lessons.fix: Choose goal cells only at the requester's floor height, cache failed goals for a few seconds and back off to local steering meanwhile, snap targets to free floor, and keep the current grid chunk cached during a search.
lessons.test: Put a goal on an unreachable roof and measure frame time and searches per second (152 ms down to 1.5 ms per frame here).

lessons.title: Reuse identical expensive queries within one frame or physics tick
lessons.symptom: A parked, occupied cockpit ran at 81 to 92 fps with nothing happening; reusing the queries gave 260 fps.
lessons.cause: Several systems asked for the same skid and terrain samples every frame (one aircraft surface sample about seven times per tick), each running the full query.
lessons.fix: Cache the result keyed on the frame number (Engine.get_process_frames() or Engine.get_physics_frames()) plus the inputs (position, heading, loaded world and moving objects); recompute as soon as any input changes, and keep one fresh query after the body has moved.
lessons.test: Measure in alternating blocks with and without reuse, and check that the results are identical, also after the world or a moving object changes.

lessons.title: A dynamic resolution target above the frame cap drives the render scale to its minimum
lessons.symptom: The adaptive render scale slowly dropped to its lowest value and never came back, even on a fast machine.
lessons.cause: The target was 120 fps while Engine.max_fps capped the game at 117, so the scaler never measured the target minus its margin and kept lowering the scale. Its minimum also ignored the lower limit allowed in the settings.
lessons.fix: Clamp the target to Engine.max_fps when a cap is set (and to the refresh rate with vertical sync on), and use the same validated range for the minimum scale as the settings menu.
lessons.test: A probe with a cap below the target must keep the scale stable.

lessons.title: Use a grid index for nearest-segment queries over long routes
lessons.symptom: Building a road network took 18 s, also when the map opened, and a track profile solver ran for minutes.
lessons.cause: Each query scanned every waypoint of every route (some had over 1400 points), and each track point was tested against every structure constraint.
lessons.fix: Put segments into grid cells (128 m worked) and search rings of cells outward until a closer hit is impossible; keep the original order of results and the same precision so the output does not change.
lessons.test: Compare thousands of indexed answers with brute force (0 differences in 16,800 here), then time it (18.3 s to 6.2 s).

lessons.title: A large texture that holds one colour wastes video memory; use a material value
lessons.symptom: The cockpit materials used 4K albedo and roughness-metal maps that each held exactly one colour.
lessons.cause: Placeholder maps were exported and never replaced. A compressed 4096 by 4096 map with mipmaps costs about 22 MB of GPU memory for three bytes of information.
lessons.fix: Find maps with a single colour (count unique colours at full size) and replace them with albedo_color, roughness and metallic values, or give them real variation derived from the normal map.
lessons.test: A script that counts unique colours per texture at full resolution.

lessons.title: A record appended on every chunk reload grows without bound
lessons.symptom: Memory kept growing the longer a session stayed in one area.
lessons.cause: A settlement builder appended an audit entry every time a chunk was built, also when the same plan was loaded again after streaming out and in.
lessons.fix: Key such records by id (one entry per plan), or cap and rotate them.
lessons.test: Load and unload the same chunk many times and check that the record count stays the same.

lessons.title: Stop looping audio players before their scene is freed or the game quits
lessons.symptom: Quitting from the menu printed a warning that six object instances were leaked at exit.
lessons.cause: Three looping AudioStreamPlayer nodes with generated AudioStreamWAV streams were never stopped, and the quit button called quit() at once, so the audio server still held their playbacks when the tree was finalised.
lessons.fix: Stop the players in _exit_tree(). In the quit routine, stop every AudioStreamPlayer, AudioStreamPlayer2D and AudioStreamPlayer3D in the tree, let a few frames pass (about 80 ms), then call quit().
lessons.test: A headless probe that starts the sounds and quits: leaked instances went from 6 to 0.
errors: ObjectDB instances were leaked at exit

lessons.title: Read Godot's output as UTF-8 and treat its indented at: lines as part of the message above
lessons.symptom: An installer refused a correct install because of a physics notice printed at shutdown, and on Windows reading Godot's output could crash the tool.
lessons.cause: Godot prints each error or warning followed by indented at: and backtrace lines. The tool counted every at: line as an error, so a harmless Jolt warning at exit blocked. It also decoded the output with the Windows code page instead of UTF-8.
lessons.fix: Group continuation lines with the message they belong to, block only on error and script error lines (record warnings), compare with a baseline from the unchanged game, and always decode Godot's output as UTF-8.
lessons.test: Feed a captured log with warnings, errors and non-ASCII text through the parser and check the counts.
errors: job system exceeded the maximum number of jobs

lessons.title: Run the shipped pack with the matching debug binary to see why it crashes
lessons.symptom: The exported game closed without a message, and the release template gave no usable error.
lessons.cause: Release export templates print little and do not report script errors with a backtrace the way a debug build does.
lessons.fix: Start the same pack with the editor or debug binary of exactly the same Godot version, using the --main-pack and --log-file options; a hard crash then turns into a readable script error. Check release-only behaviour the other way round, on the release template itself.
lessons.test: Keep a ready-made start script for this next to the game, writing its log beside the executable.

lessons.title: Headless Godot renders nothing; use a virtual display and a software GPU for image and shader checks
lessons.symptom: A showcase capture failed in headless mode, and shader errors only showed up once a renderer was used.
lessons.cause: The headless mode uses a dummy renderer: there is no viewport texture to capture, and shader code is not compiled for a GPU, so shader errors do not show.
lessons.fix: For image and shader checks run Godot under a virtual X display with a software Vulkan driver for Forward+, or a software OpenGL driver for Compatibility. Add a negative control: a shader with a deliberate typo must be reported. Never read frame rates from software rendering.
lessons.test: The negative-control shader must produce a shader error line, and the captured image must not be empty.

lessons.title: Compile every script headless, also the ones only a flag or a test loads
lessons.symptom: A check mode that the boot script offered on a command-line flag could not run in the shipped build: its script called four helper functions that no longer existed, and nothing had noticed because nothing loaded it.
lessons.cause: Godot only parses a script when something loads it. Scripts reached through a rare flag, a QA path or a menu page that is gone are never loaded in normal play, so their parse errors stay hidden.
lessons.fix: Build a check project from the full source, give missing models empty placeholder files, load every script headless (the --check-only option per script, or a SceneTree script that loads each file and records failures), and compare the error list with a stored baseline so only new errors block.
lessons.test: The check must fail on a deliberately broken copy of one script.

lessons.title: Test patches that stack in several orders, and guard rollbacks against later installs
lessons.symptom: Install kits that each passed alone failed together: one stopped because its anchor was not found, one added a second copy of a function another kit had added, one could not parse a catalogue another kit had rewritten, and one rollback silently removed a later install.
lessons.cause: An anchor assumed a list ended with one particular key; an existence check searched for a string that also occurred elsewhere; a JSON rewrite escaped every non-ASCII character and changed the end of the file; and rollback cut the pack back to its old length, which also removes everything appended after it.
lessons.fix: Run every kit on the output of the others, in several orders and on old and new bases. Match anchors by content, extend an existing function instead of adding a second one, rewrite shared data files with their original encoding, escapes, indentation and final newline, and let rollback refuse when the pack's size or directory offset differs from what the install left.
lessons.test: A stack test (here five orders on two bases) that checks every key after each step and searches for duplicate functions, constants and buttons; a rollback out of order must be refused.

lessons.title: Key installs and their tests on content, not on a version label or on what is new
lessons.symptom: Two different builds carried the same version label, so the installer skipped one as already installed; an older install was never upgraded; models replaced by an update were never loaded in the install test.
lessons.cause: The skip logic compared only a label or a step name, and the load test only covered catalogue entries that were new.
lessons.fix: Record what each step installed with a version derived from its content, skip only on an exact match, and run the load test on every resource a step adds or replaces.
lessons.test: Install the old version, upgrade, check that the replaced models load, then install again and expect no change.

lessons.title: Test new features through the entry point players actually use
lessons.symptom: Several aircraft added by install kits could not be chosen in the game, and a release check ran for three minutes without running a single test.
lessons.cause: The kits added their buttons to older menu pages that the new main menu no longer opened, and the check's command-line hook lived in an old entry script while the project now started from another boot scene.
lessons.fix: Drive smoke tests from the real main scene and menu by pressing the visible buttons, and make every check print an explicit start marker so a run without it fails.
lessons.test: A smoke test that starts from the main scene, walks the visible menu and reaches each new feature.

lessons.title: A fake host must start empty, like the real one
lessons.symptom: An adapter passed its kit test but raised two script errors per second in the game before a mission was accepted, and it built incident scenes at route waypoints.
lessons.cause: The fake session had a destination from the start, while the real session is empty until it begins, so reading the last destination of an empty array failed. The fake also had no separate waypoint and target, which hid that the adapter used the wrong one.
lessons.fix: Give the fake the real object's shape, including its empty and in-between states (before the start, between waypoints, after completion), treat empty data as inactive in the code, and fail the test on any script error in the log.
lessons.test: Add cases for no mission yet and between waypoints.

lessons.title: Store a fixed calibration workload with every performance gate result
lessons.symptom: A 2 ms performance gate failed and passed on the same code, and a stress gate went red on a slow virtual machine.
lessons.cause: Timing on a shared machine swung more than the gate's margin: the same old code measured 1.47 to 2.28 ms in single windows, and the machine's speed was not recorded with the result.
lessons.fix: Use a fixed random seed, take the median of three measuring windows, run old and new code alternately, and record a fixed calibration task (a constant script workload) with every result so a slow machine is visible next to the numbers.
lessons.test: Report the calibration time with each run and reject comparisons where it differs a lot.

lessons.title: Measure texture content at full resolution, not on a resized copy
lessons.symptom: A review concluded that a set of normal maps was nearly flat and should be replaced; they were fine.
lessons.cause: The amplitude was measured on a 96 by 96 resize of a 4096 map, and resizing averages away exactly the fine relief a normal map holds: the largest deviation looked like 3 instead of 70.
lessons.fix: Measure on the full image (unique colours, percentiles, standard deviation) and state in the report how the numbers were measured.
lessons.test: Compare the statistic on the full image and on the resize for one map before trusting a quick check.

lessons.title: Count changed frames in a player's video to find the real frame rate
lessons.symptom: A player reported that new volumetric clouds were very buggy; the 30 fps recording looked fluid at first sight.
lessons.cause: Screen recorders write frames at a fixed rate and repeat the last image when the game delivers none.
lessons.fix: Diff consecutive video frames and count real changes: 98 changes in 388 frames meant about 8 fps, with freezes of up to 20 frames (0.67 s). Measure the same views in the game again after the fix.
lessons.test: A script that reports changed frames per second and the longest run of identical frames.

lessons.title: Keep the exact source of every script you ship
lessons.symptom: Shipped builds could not be fully compile-checked or patched: one base script existed only in compiled form in the pack, and every script that extended it failed in a check project.
lessons.cause: A pack can hold scripts only as compiled tokens. Once the source is lost there is no way to review, diff or rebuild them, and a stand-in without all members breaks every subclass.
lessons.fix: Archive the exact sources with each build (or export scripts as text), record which compiled file came from which source, and when a base script cannot be shared, keep a stand-in that declares its full API.
lessons.test: Rebuild a check project from the archive alone and compile every script.

lessons.title: An index into a constant empty array stops the whole script from loading
lessons.symptom: A generated script that worked with data failed to load once its constant list was empty, with a parse error on every line that read an element, even lines that never run.
lessons.cause: Godot folds constants while it parses: reading an element of a constant array that is empty is checked then, not at run time, so it is a parse error for the whole script.
lessons.fix: Use a var for a list that can be empty, or guard the read so it only exists when the list has elements (generate the code only when there is data).
lessons.test: Load the script with the list empty and with one element, headless, and check that both load.

lessons.title: remove_child() without queue_free() leaves an orphan node on every reload
lessons.symptom: Memory and the orphan node count grew a little every time a level chunk was loaded and unloaded. At exit Godot printed that object instances were leaked.
lessons.cause: A node taken out of the tree with remove_child() is not freed. It stays alive as an orphan with all its children and resources, and freeing the scene it came from does not free it, because it is no longer a child of that scene.
lessons.fix: Call queue_free() on a node you remove and do not add back. If you keep it on purpose (a screen you swap in and out), keep it in a variable and free it in _exit_tree() of the owner, or hide it instead of removing it.
lessons.test: Load, run and free the scene several times headless and check that the orphan node count stays the same after every cycle.
errors: ObjectDB instances were leaked at exit
Leaked instances typically happen when nodes are removed from the scene tree

lessons.title: Nodes a scene adds to the root or an autoload survive when the scene is freed
lessons.symptom: After loading and leaving a level a few times, the root of the tree held more and more extra nodes: effects, timers and helpers from levels that were long gone.
lessons.cause: A level added nodes to get_tree().root or to an autoload, so they were not children of the level. Freeing or changing the scene frees only its own children.
lessons.fix: Add such nodes under the level itself when they belong to it. When they must live elsewhere, keep a reference and queue_free() them in the level's _exit_tree().
lessons.test: Free the scene, wait one frame and count the nodes under the root; the count must be the same after every load and unload.

lessons.title: A static var or autoload array keeps resources alive across reloads
lessons.symptom: Memory kept growing with every chunk reload, yet Godot reported no leaked objects at exit and the loaded-resource monitor stayed flat.
lessons.cause: Each chunk appended a material, mesh or data object to a static var or an autoload array. The array keeps them alive for the whole session; they are freed only when the game quits, so the exit report never lists them, and resources made in code are not counted by the loaded-resource monitor.
lessons.fix: Key such caches by id so a reload reuses the entry, cap their size, or remove a chunk's entries when the chunk is freed.
lessons.test: Load and unload the same chunk many times and check that the number of live objects stays the same after every cycle.

lessons.title: Object.new() is never freed on its own
lessons.symptom: The object count grew by a few every time a system ran, and the exit report listed leaked instances of class Object.
lessons.cause: A plain Object (and every class that extends Object but not RefCounted or Node) is not reference counted. Dropping the last variable that points to it does not free it.
lessons.fix: Call free() on it when done, or extend RefCounted instead so it is freed when nothing refers to it any more.
lessons.test: Run the code in a loop headless and check that the object count does not grow per loop; with --verbose, the exit report must not list class Object.
errors: ObjectDB instances were leaked at exit

lessons.title: In Godot 4.7 writing one element of a packed array property changes a copy
lessons.symptom: After the move to Godot 4.7 a line, polygon or gradient stopped updating: code that wrote one point of it ran without an error, but the node kept the old points. A script variable with a setter changed, but the work in its setter (a redraw, a signal) no longer happened.
lessons.cause: Since Godot 4.7, writing one element of a packed array no longer calls the setter of the whole property. An engine property hands out a copy of its array, so the write lands in the copy and is lost; a script variable is changed in place, without its setter.
lessons.fix: Copy the array into a local variable, change the copy, and assign the whole array back to the property. Do the same for a script variable whose setter must run.
lessons.test: Print the element after the write: in Godot 4.7 a point of a Line2D written through its points property stays at its old value until the whole array is assigned.

lessons.title: An override without a return type inherits the parent's in Godot 4.7
lessons.symptom: Scripts that loaded in Godot 4.6 stopped with a parse error in 4.7 on overrides such as _get(), _set() or _get_configuration_warnings() that only did some work and returned nothing.
lessons.cause: Since Godot 4.7 an override without a return type takes the return type of the method it overrides, also of engine virtual methods. A body that does not return a value on every path is then an error, and a bare return in a method that returns bool is one too.
lessons.fix: Return a value of the parent's type on every path: false for bool, an empty array for an array, null only where the parent returns Variant or an object.
lessons.test: Run the Godot check after the upgrade: every override it reports with this message needs a return value.
errors: Not all code paths return a value

lessons.title: RichTextLabel image size flags became an enum in Godot 4.7
lessons.symptom: A script that passed true or false for the percent flags of add_image() or update_image() stopped loading in Godot 4.7, although the upgrade guide lists the change as compatible.
lessons.cause: The two percent flags became unit parameters of type RichTextLabel.ImageUnit, and typed GDScript does not turn a bool into that enum.
lessons.fix: Pass RichTextLabel.IMAGE_UNIT_PIXEL for false and IMAGE_UNIT_PERCENT for true.

lessons.title: Keyboard and mouse events are no longer device 0 in Godot 4.7
lessons.symptom: After the move to Godot 4.7 keyboard and mouse input for the first local player stopped working, while the first gamepad still worked.
lessons.cause: Godot 4.7 gives keyboard events the device InputEvent.DEVICE_ID_KEYBOARD and mouse events DEVICE_ID_MOUSE, because a gamepad can be device 0 too. Code that took device 0 to mean keyboard and mouse no longer matches them.
lessons.fix: Test the event type, or compare the device with InputEvent.DEVICE_ID_KEYBOARD and DEVICE_ID_MOUSE; keep device numbers for gamepads.

lessons.title: Under Jolt the distance of a world boundary plane flipped in Godot 4.7
lessons.symptom: After the move to Godot 4.7 with the Jolt engine, bodies fell through the floor or rested above it where a world boundary shape used a plane distance other than zero.
lessons.cause: Godot 4.7 makes Jolt read the plane distance of a world boundary shape the way the built-in engine does, which is the opposite sign of what Jolt used in 4.6.
lessons.fix: Flip the sign of the plane distance on every world boundary shape, or move the static body instead and keep the distance at zero.
lessons.test: Drop a ball onto the boundary and print where it rests: it must rest on the side and at the height you meant.

lessons.title: Transparent objects draw through volumetric clouds when the composite plane has a lower render priority
lessons.symptom: Transparent objects such as landing zones and fade planes were visible through the cloud layer. A blue sea quad drew over the clouds.
lessons.cause: The water and cloud composite had the same or wrong render priority. The water drew after the composite and appeared on top.
lessons.fix: Set the cloud composite plane to RENDER_PRIORITY_MIN+1 and any other transparent surface (water, fade zones) to RENDER_PRIORITY_MIN. Objects that draw after the composite appear above the clouds.
lessons.test: Fly above the cloud layer and check that no transparent object pokes through it.

lessons.title: CPUParticles3D with StandardMaterial3D and vertex_color_use_as_albedo render black in Godot 4.7
lessons.symptom: Snow particles from a moving object rendered completely black.
lessons.cause: StandardMaterial3D with vertex_color_use_as_albedo on CPUParticles3D produces black pixels in Godot 4.7.
lessons.fix: Use a custom ShaderMaterial on the particles instead of StandardMaterial3D with vertex_color_use_as_albedo. The combination does not work reliably with CPUParticles3D in Godot 4.7.
lessons.test: Spawn CPUParticles3D with a white StandardMaterial3D and vertex_color_use_as_albedo true. Check that they are visible and not black.

lessons.title: Check file hashes before applying a patch to detect changes made by another agent
lessons.symptom: Multiple agents working on the same game overwrote each other's changes when patching.
lessons.cause: Patches were applied blindly without checking whether the target files had changed since the previous patch.
lessons.fix: Store the md5 of every file you replace. Before the next patch, check that the live files still have the same md5. If they differ, someone else changed them: stop and report.
lessons.test: Apply two patches that touch the same file. The second must fail with a drift warning instead of silently overwriting.

lessons.title: The player's own vehicle glows through fog when the fog shader does not exclude it
lessons.symptom: Flying through clouds made the rotor disc, cockpit glass and lamps of the player's own vehicle unnaturally bright.
lessons.cause: The fog shader treated the player's own vehicle the same as the rest of the world. Emissive materials radiated through the fog.
lessons.fix: Put the player's own vehicle on a separate visual layer that the fog shader excludes, or dim the emission of own parts when the camera is inside the cloud layer.
lessons.test: Fly through a cloud layer and check that the player's own vehicle does not become brighter than the surroundings.

lessons.title: A navigation lock needs a waiting area, door timers, a water level and signal lights to work
lessons.symptom: Locks without a proper cycle let ships sail straight through as if no lock existed, or ships got stuck.
lessons.cause: The lock had no state machine for the locking cycle: no waiting area, no door timers, no water level.
lessons.fix: Implement a full locking cycle: a waiting area at a distance from the lock, doors with an open time, chamber water with a fill level, lights per lock head (red/red+green/green), an emergency stop after a timeout. Let one ship through at a time.
lessons.test: Run 19+ locks with test ships over 1500 seconds. Check: 0 emergency stops, 0 stuck ships.

lessons.title: Vertex colours (COLOR_0) from a glTF are not rendered by Godot's runtime GLTF loader
lessons.symptom: Baked ambient occlusion via vertex colours was invisible after the model was loaded with the runtime GLTF loader, even with the correct material flags.
lessons.cause: Godot's runtime GLTFDocument loader does not render vertex colours (COLOR_0), even with vertex_color_use_as_albedo or an uncompressed rebuilt model.
lessons.fix: Do not use baked AO via vertex colours when the model is loaded with GLTFDocument at runtime. Bake AO into a texture or use screen-space AO instead.
lessons.test: Load a GLB with vertex colours via GLTFDocument. Check whether the colours are visible in the viewport.

lessons.title: A doubled coordinate offset in a model generator makes the model metres too long
lessons.symptom: A generated aircraft was 67.9 m long instead of 48.5 m, with a beam sticking 20 m in front of the nose.
lessons.cause: The generator added a part's z coordinate twice, pushing a component far in front of the model.
lessons.fix: Check the total bounding box of the generated model against the specification after every generation run. If the size deviates by more than 1 percent, look for doubled offsets in the generator.
lessons.test: Measure the bounding box of the generated model and compare with the specification. Deviation must be under 1 percent.

lessons.title: A cockpit canopy that is too tight around the head feels claustrophobic; measure the headroom
lessons.symptom: The cockpit canopy ran at eye level along the head, making it feel cramped and pushing the camera against the glass.
lessons.cause: The canopy was too low and too narrow. The roof arch sat above the eye instead of behind it.
lessons.fix: Make the canopy taller and wider than the head (at least 15 to 20 cm of headroom). Check that the roof arch is behind the eye, not above it. Measure the distance from the eye point to the nearest canopy surface.
lessons.test: Measure the distance from the eye point to the nearest canopy surface. Minimum 15 cm.

lessons.title: A moving AudioStreamPlayer3D needs an AudioListener3D or the doppler shift uses the wrong reference
lessons.symptom: Engine sounds had no doppler shift, or the shift was backwards when the camera moved.
lessons.cause: Without an explicit AudioListener3D the engine uses the Camera3D. When the camera and the source move together (cockpit view), there is no relative velocity and no shift.
lessons.fix: Place an AudioListener3D at the listener position (the camera or the player's head). For doppler on the player's own engine, put the listener on a fixed ground point or at the camera only when it does not ride the vehicle.
lessons.test: Fly past a fixed observer with a tone. The pitch must rise on approach and fall on departure.

lessons.title: Rain and snow particles must move with the camera or they fall behind at speed
lessons.symptom: At speed, rain and snow streaked backwards and left empty air in front of the vehicle.
lessons.cause: The particle emitter was placed at a fixed world position. At 100+ m/s the camera outruns the emitter volume.
lessons.fix: Parent the emitter to the camera and use local_coords = false so particles keep their world velocity after emission. Offset the emission box forward by half the speed times the particle lifetime.
lessons.test: Fly at top speed in rain. Particles must fill the view, not trail behind.

lessons.title: A cockpit at night is invisible unless instrument panels have emissive or backlit materials
lessons.symptom: At night the cockpit was completely black. Only the HUD glass showed anything.
lessons.cause: The instruments and panels used only albedo with no emission, so without ambient or fill light they were invisible.
lessons.fix: Add a subtle emission texture to lit instrument faces and backlit panels. Keep the emission strength low (0.5 to 1.5) so it does not wash out. Use an OmniLight3D with a short range for the red cockpit flood light.
lessons.test: Render the cockpit at midnight with no moon. Every instrument must be readable.

lessons.title: A wheeled vehicle on a moving deck rolls away unless its brakes counter the deck acceleration
lessons.symptom: Parked vehicles rolled off a ship's deck in turns and in waves.
lessons.cause: The wheels had no brake force applied when parked. The deck accelerated under them (turn, pitch, roll) and the wheels followed the deck surface but were free to roll.
lessons.fix: Apply a brake torque that exceeds the maximum deck acceleration times the wheel radius times the vehicle mass. Also chock the wheels by setting wheel friction to a high value when parked.
lessons.test: Park on a deck at maximum turn rate and in rough seas for 60 seconds. The vehicle must not move more than 5 cm.

lessons.title: Buildings at chunk borders pop when one chunk loads a different LOD than its neighbour
lessons.symptom: Buildings near chunk edges flickered between high and low detail when the camera moved.
lessons.cause: Each chunk decided its LOD independently. A building at the border of two chunks got different LODs from each, and the switch was not synchronised.
lessons.fix: Decide LOD per object, not per chunk. Use the 3D distance from the camera to each building, with a hysteresis band so it does not switch back and forth. Use VISIBILITY_RANGE_FADE_SELF for smooth fading.
lessons.test: Walk along a chunk border and check that no building changes detail level abruptly.

lessons.title: An NPC boarding sequence must wait for the door animation and check that the door is open
lessons.symptom: NPCs walked through closed doors or got stuck waiting for a door that was already open.
lessons.cause: The boarding code started walking to the seat as soon as the door was requested, without waiting for it to finish opening. Another path skipped the check entirely.
lessons.fix: Wait for the door animation to finish (connect to the animation_finished signal), then check that the door angle exceeds a threshold before sending the NPC through. Add a timeout: if the door does not open within 5 seconds, try an alternative entrance.
lessons.test: Run the boarding with the door jammed half open, fully open, and stuck closed. The NPC must wait, walk through, and reroute respectively.

lessons.title: A Decal parented to a moving object must have its cull_mask set to include that object's layer
lessons.symptom: Tyre marks and damage decals did not appear on a moving ship's deck.
lessons.cause: The Decal's cull_mask did not include the deck's render layer, so the projector never hit it.
lessons.fix: Set the Decal's cull_mask to include the render layer of the surface it projects onto. For a moving surface, parent the Decal to the moving object so it moves with it.
lessons.test: Place a decal on a moving deck and check it stays in place and is visible.

lessons.title: A static var that caches a node reference keeps pointing to a freed node after the scene changes
lessons.symptom: After leaving a level, the cached node was freed but the static var still pointed to it, causing errors on the next access.
lessons.cause: A static var or class variable cached a node reference. When the scene was freed, the node was freed but the variable still held it.
lessons.fix: Clear cached node references in _exit_tree(). Use a WeakRef or check is_instance_valid() before every access. Better: use groups or signals instead of caching node references across scene changes.
lessons.test: Load and unload a scene twice. Access the cached node after unload. It must not error.

lessons.title: A procedural town generator must place buildings and roads from the same grid or they misalign
lessons.symptom: Buildings stood in the middle of roads, and roads cut through buildings.
lessons.cause: The road generator and the building generator used different grids and did not share footprint data.
lessons.fix: Generate roads first, store their footprints, then place buildings in the remaining space. Use one shared grid for both. Check for overlaps after generation.
lessons.test: Generate a town and count building-road overlaps. Must be zero.

lessons.title: Train cars coupled with joints must have matching physics priorities or the train snakes
lessons.symptom: A train of five cars snaked sideways at speed and derailed in curves.
lessons.cause: Each car updated its physics in arbitrary order. The locomotive pulled, the first car responded a tick later, and so on, so the whole train was never in equilibrium.
lessons.fix: Set process_physics_priority so the locomotive runs first and each following car after it in order. Use a stiff joint or custom code with damping. Limit the angle between cars.
lessons.test: Run a 5-car train at top speed through a curve. No car may leave the track.

lessons.title: A round minimap drawn as a full rectangle on a high canvas layer hides everything behind it
lessons.symptom: Buttons and indicators near the minimap corner were unclickable because the minimap's invisible rectangle covered them.
lessons.cause: The minimap used a TextureRect the full size of its canvas, with a circular shader mask. The invisible area still received mouse input.
lessons.fix: Set mouse_filter to MOUSE_FILTER_IGNORE on the minimap container, or use MOUSE_FILTER_PASS and handle clicks only inside the circle. Size the control to the visible circle, not the full corner.
lessons.test: Click a button that sits behind the minimap's transparent area. It must respond.

lessons.title: Shadow cascade boundaries jitter at high speed when the camera moves faster than one cascade width per frame
lessons.symptom: Shadows flickered and jumped at high speed, with visible lines where cascades met.
lessons.cause: At 200+ m/s the camera moved the full width of a cascade in a few frames. The cascade split points snapped to texel grid positions, causing visible jumps.
lessons.fix: Stabilise cascade splits by rounding the camera position to the texel size of each cascade. Increase the overlap between cascades. At very high speed, switch to a single cascade with a large range and accept softer shadows.
lessons.test: Fly at top speed along the ground. Shadows must not flicker or show cascade boundaries.
